AI.method: FASR++ is a diffusion-model-based SR framework that uses a reference low-resolution image and features extracted from multiple auxiliary low-quality frames to generate a high-quality SR output; it avoids explicit soft-attribute conditioning and gradient guidance and serves as a pre-processing step to improve recognition performance.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art results for verification, face recognition, and image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) on two standard datasets.
AI.conclusion: Multi-frame diffusion-based SR can substantially improve surveillance face recognition by producing identity-preserving high-quality reconstructions, suitable as an effective pre-processing step.

title: Auto-DSM Under the Lens: A Black-Box Evaluation Framework for LLM-Based DSM Generation
summary: This paper presents a black-box evaluation framework to systematically assess the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate Design Structure Matrices (DSMs) from structured technical documentation. Motivated by the closed-source nature of current Auto-DSM pipelines, the framework introduces a reproducible methodology that benchmarks generated DSMs (GEN-DSMs) against manually validated ground-truth matrices (GT-DSMs). The evaluation integrates both single-run and multi-run perspectives, combining structural metrics (Completeness, Correctness, Coupling Density), classification metrics (Selective Accuracy, Abstention Coverage), and stability measures (Entropy, Fleiss' $κ$). To synthesize these aspects, a Composite Quality Score (Q) is proposed. Controlled experiments are conducted on two datasets: a fictive abstract system and a real-world refrigerator decomposition, covering variations in phrasing, parameter-dataset alignment, and system complexity. Results show that LLMs can produce structurally plausible DSMs and achieve high reproducibility under well-structured inputs, but remain sensitive to ambiguity, inconsistent dependency definitions, and prompt formulation. The findings highlight systematic sources of hallucination and abstention failure, demonstrating both the potential and current limitations of LLM-driven DSM automation. The proposed framework provides a transparent benchmark for auditing Auto-DSM pipelines and establishes foundations for integrating LLM-based decomposition methods into model-based systems engineering (MBSE) workflows.

AI.tldr: A reproducible black-box framework to evaluate LLM-generated Design Structure Matrices (DSMs) against ground-truth DSMs, using structural, classification, and stability metrics, plus a composite quality score. Demonstrates LLMs can produce plausible DSMs and be reproducible with well-structured prompts, but are sensitive to ambiguity and prompt design; provides a benchmark for Auto-DSM and MBSE integration.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of transparent, reproducible benchmarking for Auto-DSM pipelines and assess whether LLMs can generate valid DSMs from structured documentation.
AI.method: A black-box evaluation framework comparing GEN-DSMs to manually validated GT-DSMs across single and multi-run settings. Metrics include structural (Completeness, Correctness, Coupling Density), classification (Selective Accuracy, Abstention Coverage), and stability (Entropy, Fleiss' κ). A Composite Quality Score Q aggregates these aspects. Experiments on two datasets (a fictive abstract system and a real refrigerator decomposition) with variations in phrasing, parameter-dataset alignment, and system complexity.
AI.result: LLMs can generate structurally plausible DSMs and show high reproducibility under well-structured inputs, but performance degrades with ambiguity, inconsistent dependency definitions, and prompt misformation. The study identifies hallucination and abstention failure as systematic error modes. The framework offers a transparent benchmark for auditing Auto-DSM pipelines and supports integrating LLM-based decomposition into MBSE workflows.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark for LLM-driven DSM automation, enabling assessment of potential and limitations. It lays groundwork for integrating LLM-based decomposition methods into model-based systems engineering (MBSE) workflows, while highlighting the need for robust prompting and validation to mitigate hallucinations and abstentions.

title: MP-MPPI: A Motion Primitive Guided Sampling-Based Optimizer for Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper proposes a novel method that extends the Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) method with motion primitives for additional structured sampling, which enhances the convergence towards a globally optimal solution. By evaluating motion primitives and perturbed control sequences in a real-time sampling-based optimization loop, this work addresses the limitations of the path planning capabilities of sampling-based controllers. The algorithm is implemented on a quadcopter simulator and tested on an obstacle field navigation task. It is demonstrated that the proposed approach enhances exploration of the control space while maintaining the fast, reactive behavior required for real-time control.

AI.tldr: MPPI with motion primitives extends sampling-based planning to enable structured exploration, improving convergence toward globally better solutions in real-time obstacle avoidance on a quadcopter simulator.
AI.motivation: Address limitations of traditional sampling-based controllers in path planning; enhance exploration and convergence to near-optimal trajectories while maintaining real-time performance.
AI.method: Integrates motion primitives into the MPPI framework, evaluating primitive-based and perturbed control sequences within a real-time sampling loop for structured sampling.
AI.result: Implementation in a quadcopter simulator; obstacle field navigation tasks show improved control-space exploration while preserving fast, reactive real-time behavior.
AI.conclusion: Motion-primitives augmentation of MPPI yields better exploration and real-time feasibility for sampling-based path planning in dynamic environments.

title: A Coin Flip Per Token: Bernoulli Sparse Steering of Large Language Models
summary: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning, but standard methods apply the steering signal at every generated token, incurring constant per-token perturbation that risks degrading fluency. We ask: is dense intervention necessary? We introduce Stochastic Token Steering (STS), which gates each token independently with probability $p$, and Stochastic Block Steering (SBS), which gates a leading window once per sequence; neither requires a reward model or learned gating policy. Across two model families and two behavioral tasks, steering only 50% of the tokens recovers most of the dense-steering effect while preserving fluency, and steering as few as 30% surpasses prompt-based control. The optimal steering magnitude scales inversely with the intervention ratio, revealing that SAE-mediated control is rate-limited: the behavioral outcome depends on cumulative signal dosage across a sequence.

AI.tldr: Sparse activation steering can achieve most of the dense SAE effect with far less perturbation. STS (per-token) and SBS (leading-window) gating preserve fluency while reducing intervention, with 50% token coverage capturing most benefit and 30% surpassing prompt-based control; the optimal steering scales inversely with the intervention ratio, indicating the outcome depends on cumulative signal dosage.
AI.motivation: To reduce per-token perturbation in activation steering and preserve fluency, by testing whether sparse, stochastic interventions can match dense SAE steering without a gating policy or reward model.
AI.method: Introduce two stochastic gating schemes: Stochastic Token Steering (STS) gates each token independently with probability p; Stochastic Block Steering (SBS) gates a leading window once per sequence. No reward model or learned gating policy required. Evaluate across two model families and two behavioral tasks, comparing against dense steering.
AI.result: Steering about 50% of tokens recovers most of the dense-steering effect while preserving fluency; steering as few as 30% can surpass prompt-based control. The optimal steering magnitude scales inversely with the intervention ratio, revealing the control is rate-limited by cumulative signal dosage across a sequence.
AI.conclusion: SAE-mediated behavioral control does not require dense, per-token intervention; sparse, stochastic steering achieves comparable effects, with performance governed by the cumulative dosage of steering across a sequence and flexibility across model families and tasks.

title: Scene Graph Thinking: Reinforcing Structured Visual Reasoning for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated strong perception and reasoning capabilities. However, most existing models focus on isolated objects and neglect structured relationships for efficient target navigation, limiting their performance on visually intensive tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Scene Graph Thinking (SaGe), a novel paradigm that enables fine-grained and structured visual reasoning through explicit scene-graph representations. Specifically, we first introduce an automated data engine that converts flat image-text corpora into structured scene graphs, where hierarchical entities constitute the nodes and diverse visual relations define the edges. Building upon this, we construct 120K high-quality training data by sampling reasoning traces from scene graphs. Then, two-stage graph-aligned post-training paradigms are introduced, where supervised fine-tuning internalizes MLLMs with structured reasoning, and subsequent reinforcement fine-tuning proposes node-as-proxy graph rewards to consolidate efficient graph exploration. With curated data and graph-aligned training, our approach achieves significant improvements across eight multimodal benchmarks, demonstrating strong effectiveness on fine-grained perception and reasoning tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/zwyang6/SaGe.

AI.tldr: SaGe introduces Scene Graph Thinking to multimodal LLMs by converting image-text data into structured scene graphs, generating ~120k reasoning traces, and using a two-stage graph-aligned post-training (supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement fine-tuning with node-as-proxy graph rewards) to improve fine-grained perception and reasoning across eight multimodal benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current multimodal LLMs excel at recognizing isolated objects but struggle with structured relationships and reasoning necessary for visually intensive tasks. Explicit scene-graph representations promise fine-grained, structured reasoning and more efficient target navigation in complex scenes.
AI.method: Develop an automated data engine that converts flat image-text corpora into structured scene graphs (nodes = hierarchical entities; edges = diverse visual relations). Create ~120k high-quality training examples by sampling reasoning traces from scene graphs. Propose a two-stage graph-aligned post-training paradigm: (1) supervised fine-tuning to internalize structured reasoning within MLLMs; (2) reinforcement fine-tuning using node-as-proxy graph rewards to promote efficient graph exploration.
AI.result: The proposed SaGe framework yields significant improvements across eight multimodal benchmarks, demonstrating strong gains in fine-grained perception and structured reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Explicit scene-graph thinking enables more precise, structured visual reasoning in MLLMs. The automated data engine plus two-stage graph-aligned training effectively enhances multimodal performance, with code released for replication.

title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework
summary: LLM-agent simulations make natural-language social scenarios easy to instantiate, but their outputs can be overread as predictions and are often difficult to compare with explicit social dynamics. We present AgoraSim, a hybrid agent-based modeling framework for scenario-oriented social reaction analysis. AgoraSim resolves textual or multimodal artifacts into editable ABM configurations, runs ratio-controlled populations that mix LLM, vision-language, custom-endpoint, random, and classical agents, and compares the same scenario against matched classical reference dynamics. All agents emit a shared structured decision object, enabling common action spaces, interaction protocols, metrics, and audit records. Exposed through a local UI, Python SDK/CLI, and REST API, AgoraSim helps users inspect scenario trajectories, compare modeling assumptions, and identify cases that warrant empirical validation.

AI.tldr: AgoraSim is a hybrid ABM framework that converts textual/multimodal scenario inputs into editable agent-based models, supports mixed populations (LLMs, vision-language, custom endpoints, random, and classical agents), and enables comparison with matched classical dynamics using a shared decision object, accessible via UI, SDK/CLI, and REST for transparent scenario analysis and empirical validation.
AI.motivation: LLM-driven simulations often produce outputs treated as predictions and are hard to benchmark against explicit social dynamics. A unified framework is needed to convert textual/multimodal artifacts into controllable ABMs, enable fair comparisons to classical dynamics, and provide audit trails for validation.
AI.method: Resolve textual or multimodal artifacts into editable ABM configurations; create ratio-controlled populations mixing diverse agent types (LLM, vision-language, custom endpoints, random, classical); have all agents emit a shared structured decision object to standardize actions, protocols, metrics, and audit records; expose via local UI, Python SDK/CLI, and REST API to support scenario inspection, assumption comparison, and empirical-validation targeting.
AI.result: AgoraSim delivers a practical framework that unifies heterogeneous agent types under a common decision object, supports scenario trajectory inspection, enables comparisons against matched classical reference dynamics, and provides tools for auditing and evaluating modeling assumptions across interfaces (UI/SDK/CLI/REST).
AI.conclusion: AgoraSim enables systematic scenario-oriented social reaction analysis by bridging textual/multimodal inputs with explicit ABMs, offering standardized actions and auditability, and guiding users toward empirical validation of modeled dynamics.

title: EAGOR: Embodied Reasoning in Omni-direction
summary: Omni-directional (360°) cameras provide embodied agents with a holistic view of their surroundings, making them suited for directional reasoning in tasks such as navigation and object search. Existing Vision Language Models (VLMs) project 360° observations to 2D equirectangular projection (ERP) images and process them using architectures designed for perspective images. However, they ignore the spherical nature of 360° observations, where each pixel represents a viewing direction relative to the agent. Consequently, their direction estimates often become inconsistent under camera view transformations caused by agent motion. This limitation is particularly critical for map-free navigation, where the agent must continuously estimate the target direction in its egocentric frame. We propose EAGOR, a training-free, geometry-aware framework for embodied 360° directional reasoning. Instead of predicting target directions as ERP image coordinates, EAGOR formulates directional reasoning as recursive Bayesian estimation directly on the sphere. It maintains a continuous belief over target directions and propagates it equivariantly under agent motion without training the backbone VLMs. To achieve this, we introduce the Spherical Harmonic Belief Field (SH-BF), whose spherical harmonic representation provides a globally defined, rotation-aware basis for directional estimation on the spherical manifold. This formulation eliminates ERP seam discontinuities, latitude distortions, and interpolation errors. We evaluate EAGOR on two benchmark datasets and real-world experiments with a legged robot across directional reasoning tasks. EAGOR consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving average relative gains of +34.4% and +45.6% on HOS and OSR-Bench, respectively, while improving navigation success by +14.6%, reducing step count by 17.7%, and lowering mean angular error by 24.5%.

AI.tldr: A geometry-aware, training-free framework (EAGOR) for 360° directional reasoning on the sphere using a Spherical Harmonic Belief Field, achieving better directional estimation and navigation without retraining VLMs.
AI.motivation: Current 360° VLM pipelines project 360° views to 2D ERP images and process with perspective-oriented architectures, ignoring the spherical geometry. This leads to inconsistent direction estimates under agent motion and hampers map-free navigation.
AI.method: Formulates directional reasoning as recursive Bayesian estimation directly on the sphere. Maintains a continuous belief over target directions and propagates it equivariantly under agent motion without retraining backbone VLMs. Introduces the Spherical Harmonic Belief Field (SH-BF), whose spherical harmonic representation provides a global, rotation-aware basis on the sphere, removing ERP seams, latitude distortions, and interpolation errors.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on two benchmarks (HOS and OSR-Bench) and real-world legged-robot experiments shows strong gains: +34.4% (HOS) and +45.6% (OSR-Bench) in average relative performance. Navigation improvements include +14.6% success rate, -17.7% fewer steps, and -24.5% mean angular error.
AI.conclusion: EAGOR offers a training-free, geometry-aware solution for embodied 360° directional reasoning that outperforms existing ERP-based methods, remains robust to agent motion, and can enhance map-free navigation tasks.

title: Safe Bayesian Optimization with Counterfactual Policies
summary: In many decision-making settings, new interventions are acceptable only if they do not reduce outcomes below some established threshold. For example, in clinical medicine, new treatments are often acceptable only if they do not worsen outcomes relative to an established standard of care. Safe Bayesian optimization maximizes an objective subject to safety constraints. In the setting that we consider here, safety is defined relative to a known baseline policy whose outcomes are counterfactual and therefore unobserved. Thus, the counterfactual outcomes of the baseline policy must be estimated and those (uncertain) estimates must be used to safely optimize the objective. We address this estimation problem by using conformal prediction to construct valid uncertainty intervals for counterfactual baseline outcomes, and we show how these intervals can be integrated into safe Bayesian optimization to ensure that constraint violations occur at or below a user-specified rate. We also show how to adapt these conformal estimates to different kinds of covariate shift. We provide a safety proof, experimental evidence, and a sensitivity analysis.

AI.tldr: A safe Bayesian optimization framework that handles safety constraints defined by unobserved counterfactual baselines. It uses conformal prediction to build valid uncertainty intervals for those baselines and integrates them into the optimization to cap constraint violations at a user-specified rate, with adaptation to covariate shift and supportive theory and experiments.
AI.motivation: In many decision settings, new interventions must not worsen outcomes relative to a baseline, but the baseline outcomes are counterfactual and unobserved. This creates a challenging safety problem for optimizing interventions.
AI.method: Use conformal prediction to construct valid uncertainty intervals for counterfactual baseline outcomes. Integrate these intervals into a safe Bayesian optimization loop to ensure constraint violations occur no more than a predefined rate. Adapt the conformal estimates to different covariate shifts and provide a safety proof.
AI.result: Provides a formal safety guarantee (violations bounded by the desired rate), experimental validation showing effective safe optimization, and a sensitivity analysis assessing robustness to shifts and parameter choices.
AI.conclusion: The approach offers a practical, statistically principled means of safe optimization when the safety baseline is unobserved, with applicability to domains like clinical decision-making; extensions may address multiple constraints and scalability.

title: Association Restoration Test: Revealing Restorable Shortcuts after Unlearning
summary: Association unlearning aims to disable learned label-attribute shortcuts while preserving task performance. Existing evaluations mainly measure output-level robustness or probe whether shortcut attributes remain readable in frozen features, but neither test determines whether a retained association remains functionally usable by the original classifier. We propose the Association Restoration Test (ART), a post-hoc diagnostic for functional shortcut restorability. ART estimates class-conditional association directions, amplifies residual components, and evaluates the modified features with the original classifier head. Across Waterbirds, CelebA, SpuCoDogs, and an ISIC timestamp-artifact extension, we show that output metrics, representation probes, and ART characterize distinct aspects of shortcut mitigation. These findings motivate restoration-aware evaluation for unlearning and shortcut-mitigation methods that target learned associations rather than individual classes or concepts.

AI.tldr: Introduces Association Restoration Test (ART) to diagnose functional restorability of learned shortcuts after unlearning; ART complements output metrics and probes by testing whether residual associations can be reinstated using the original classifier head.
AI.motivation: Current unlearning evaluations focus on output robustness or representation readability but do not assess whether remaining associations remain functionally usable by the classifier; a diagnostic is needed to measure functional restorability of shortcuts.
AI.method: Estimate class-conditional association directions, amplify residual components, and evaluate the modified features with the original classifier head to assess if shortcuts can be functionally reinstated.
AI.result: ART, together with existing metrics (output metrics and probes), characterizes distinct aspects of shortcut mitigation across Waterbirds, CelebA, SpuCoDogs, and ISIC timestamp-artifact extension; shows that restoration-aware evaluation is valuable for unlearning methods.
AI.conclusion: Future unlearning and shortcut-mitigation research should target learned associations themselves (not only class-level or concept-level features) and adopt restoration-aware diagnostics like ART to determine functional usability of residual associations.

title: Information Limits and Attractor Dynamics in Economies of Frontier LLM Agents: A Pre-Registered Test
comment: 15 pages. Preprint. Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21185866. Companion synthesis: arXiv:2606.12502
summary:
We report a pre-registered, two-part experiment on small economies of frontier language-model agents (Claude Opus 4.8), testing two quantitative predictions about coupled multi-agent systems: an information-theoretic capacity region for wealth growth under market coupling, and a mean-field residual-scaling law for population misalignment under incentive and control levers. All predictions, acceptance bands, and decision rules were frozen in a public git chain before any run; every reported number re-derives mechanically from cached model outputs; the entire experiment cost $138.76 in metered API spend and is re-runnable at zero cost from the cache.
  Result 1 (confirmation): in parimutuel-coupled economies, relative growth equals relative claimed information -- the gap law G_a - G_b = I_a - I_b holds to a worst-case 46 millinats (pre-registered band: 50) across four perception structures; coalition value is submodular exactly where channels are conditionally independent, and a designed XOR synergy control flips it supermodular by 0.62 >= ln2/2 nats, with agents reasoning out the joint bit; the joint growth ceiling G_S <= H(X) binds exactly; and the best-informed agent absorbs essentially the whole wealth pool in 4/5 market seeds.
  Result 2 (structural negative): the residual-scaling test returned "domain not found." In all 72 population runs, goal dispersion collapsed (V -> 0; maximum 4.85 against a frozen floor of 5.31), the population's response to the two levers was a step function across the dominance boundary rather than a smooth response, and cells near the boundary were bistable with seed-selected outcomes. No tested LLM population at any capability level realizes the noise-maintained-dispersion regime the smooth mean-field model assumes. We release the full protocol, pre-registration chain, call cache, and analysis code.

AI.tldr: Two-part, pre-registered experiment on frontier LLM agents tests information-theoretic wealth-growth bounds under parimutuel coupling and a mean-field residual-scaling law under incentives; results: partial confirmation of capacity/ordering predictions, and a robust structural negative showing the smooth dispersion regime does not emerge in tested populations; full protocol and data released.
AI.motivation: To understand how coupled multi-agent economies based on large language models behave under information-theoretic constraints and under incentive/control levers, and to test the applicability of mean-field analyses in finite, heterogeneous, domain-locked agent populations.
AI.method: Pre-registered two-part experiment using Claude Opus 4.8 in parimutuel-coupled economies. Four perception structures, 72 population runs, frozen bands and decision rules, cache-based re-runs of all results, and public Git-based pre-registration, call cache, and analysis code. Predictions include an information-theoretic capacity region for wealth growth and a mean-field residual-scaling law for population misalignment.
AI.result: Result 1 (confirmation): relative growth equals relative claimed information (G_a - G_b = I_a - I_b) holds within 46 millinats of a pre-registered 50-nat band; coalition value submodular when channels are conditionally independent; XOR synergy control yields a supermodular gain; joint growth ceiling G_S <= H(X) binds exactly; best-informed agent absorbs most wealth in 4/5 seeds. Result 2 (negative): residual-scaling test produced domain not found; dispersion collapses (V -> 0) with a step-function response to levers; boundary cells are bistable; no tested population realizes the smooth noise-maintained-dispersion regime. Full protocol and data released.
AI.conclusion: The study provides partial empirical validation for the information-theoretic predictions of wealth growth under parimutuel coupling and reveals structural limitations of the mean-field residual-scaling law in practical LLM-population regimes. It highlights the necessity of finite-population, dependence-aware analyses and offers openly available data/code for replication.

title: Calf-Integrated Arms for Bimanual Quadruped Loco-Manipulation
summary: Most quadruped loco-manipulation designs trade manipulation capability against stance. A trunk-mounted arm sits high and usually carries a single arm; using the legs as manipulators lifts the manipulating leg off the ground; and even leg-mounted grippers reach two-handed tasks only by rearing onto the hind legs. This paper integrates a manipulator with a prismatic slider, two revolute joints, and a gripper into each front calf of a Unitree Go2. The two arms grasp objects at ground level and manipulate with both hands while all four feet stay planted, without rearing. With one arm carrying, the base stays free to walk. A vision-language model sequences skills from a predefined library at each skill boundary, conditioned on the head-camera image and task state, for long-horizon autonomy. In simulation, the design performs three bimanual tasks: a long-horizon cabinet task under autonomous skill selection, a cooperative two-handed lift, and an inter-arm handover.

AI.tldr: A quadruped robot (Unitree Go2) integrates dual ground-level arms into each front calf for stance-preserving manipulation, enabling bimanual tasks without rearing and autonomous long-horizon skill execution via a vision-language planner.
AI.motivation: To overcome the manipulation-vs-stance trade-off in quadruped locomotion by embedding low-profile, ground-level manipulation in the forelimbs, allowing simultaneous locomotion and manipulation without sacrificing stability.
AI.method: Install a prismatic slider, two revolute joints, and a gripper as part of each front calf. The two arms grasp at ground level while four feet remain planted; with one arm carrying, the base remains free to walk. A vision-language model sequences skills from a predefined library at skill boundaries, conditioned on head-camera image and task state, enabling long-horizon autonomy.
AI.result: In simulation, the design achieves three bimanual tasks: (1) a long-horizon cabinet task with autonomous skill selection, (2) a cooperative two-handed lift, and (3) an inter-arm handover. The system can perform these tasks while maintaining stance, and the base can continue walking with one arm carrying a payload.
AI.conclusion: Ground-level, dual-arm manipulation integrated into a quadruped forelimb enables stable stance-preserving manipulation and autonomous long-horizon task execution, demonstrated in simulation across coordinated bimanual tasks.

title: Intuitionistic Fuzzy Graph Embedded Random Vector Functional Link with Multiview Learning
summary: Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL) networks are popular due to their fast training and universal approximation capabilities. However, RVFL models face challenges in preserving geometric relationships and utilizing multiple feature views effectively. To address these limitations we propose the Intuitionistic Fuzzy Graph Embedded Random Vector Functional Link with Multiview Learning (IFGRVFL-MV) model. The proposed approach comprises three key components: intuitionistic fuzzy sets for uncertainty handling, graph embedding to capture intrinsic geometric structures, and multiview learning to use complementary information from multiple feature spaces. The model assigns intuitionistic fuzzy membership and non-membership values to data points making it robust to outliers. Also, the graph embedding framework preserves topological structures, increasing the generalization performance. We performed experiments on benchmark datasets from UCI and KEEL repositories which concludes that IFGRVFL-MV outperforms existing models in classification accuracy. Our results establish that IFGRVFL-MV is a promising advancement in the domain of uncertainty and multiview environments.

AI.tldr: IFGRVFL-MV: a novel RVFL-based framework that integrates intuitionistic fuzzy sets, graph embedding, and multiview learning to better handle uncertainty, preserve geometry, and fuse multiple feature views, achieving superior classification accuracy on UCI/KEEL benchmarks.
AI.motivation: RVFL networks train quickly and have universal approximation, but struggle to maintain geometric relations and exploit multiple feature views. Incorporating uncertainty handling (intuitionistic fuzzy sets), geometry-aware graph embedding, and multiview fusion aims to enhance robustness and generalization.
AI.method: Introduce intuitionistic fuzzy membership and non-membership for data points; apply graph embedding to preserve intrinsic topological structure; employ multiview learning to fuse information from multiple feature spaces within an RVFL framework (IFGRVFL-MV). Train and evaluate on UCI and KEEL benchmark datasets.
AI.result: IFGRVFL-MV outperforms existing models in classification accuracy on the benchmark datasets, indicating improved robustness to outliers and better generalization via geometry-preserving and multiview fusion strategies.
AI.conclusion: IFGRVFL-MV is a promising direction for uncertainty-aware and multiview-enabled RVFL frameworks, offering improved performance and generalization for classification tasks.

title: SAMPLe: SAM-based Optimizer for Prompt Learning in VLMs
comment: The manuscript has been accepted to ECCV and will be presented at the conference and published in the main proceedings
summary: Pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP have proven highly effective as foundation models for various downstream applications. However, prompt learning in VLMs encounters a performance-generalization dilemma: while prompts can be tuned to achieve high accuracy on seen distributions, this tuning process often undermines their generalizability to unseen data. The limited set of learnable prompts, which contextualize and condition the input to steer it toward the task within the pretrained VLM, tends to overfit the training data, leading to a trade-off between task-specific performance and preserving generalization. To address this dilemma, we introduce SAMPLe (Sharpness-Aware Minimization Prompt Learning), a plug-in sharpness-aware optimizer that enhances prompt generalizability by accounting for loss landscape sharpness. Unlike conventional methods, SAMPLe balances exploration and exploitation by satisfying objective function constraints at each step, dynamically adapting to the current optimization state based on the local curvature and gradient properties. This approach reduces overfitting on seen distributions and improves adaptability to unseen data, preserving the generalization potential of pre-trained VLM models. We integrate SAMPLe into multiple prompt learning frameworks, including CoOp, CoCoOp, MaPLe, TCP, and Co-Prompt, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse methods. Experiments show that SAMPLe elevates prompt learning frameworks and consistently outperforms existing optimizers across diverse settings, establishing itself as a robust, model-agnostic solution for prompt learning.

AI.tldr: Proposes SAMPLe, a sharpness-aware prompt-learning optimizer that improves generalization in vision-language models by mitigating overfitting; it plugs into multiple prompt-learning frameworks and yields consistent gains over existing optimizers.
AI.motivation: Prompt learning in VLMs tends to overfit to seen distributions, sacrificing generalization to unseen data; a method to directly manage loss landscape sharpness is needed.
AI.method: Introduce SAMPLe, a plug-in sharpness-aware optimizer that accounts for local curvature and gradient properties; dynamically balances exploration and exploitation by enforcing objective constraints at each step; adaptable to current optimization state; integrates with CoOp, CoCoOp, MaPLe, TCP, Co-Prompt.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations show SAMPLe consistently improves performance of various prompt-learning frameworks across diverse settings, outperforming existing optimizers; robust and model-agnostic.
AI.conclusion: SAMPLe provides a robust, generalizable solution for prompt learning in VLMs by controlling loss sharpness, enabling better generalization to unseen data while maintaining task performance.

title: PolyWorkBench: Benchmarking Multilingual Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong performance in long-horizon tasks that require planning, tool use, and interaction with external environments. However, most existing benchmarks implicitly assume a monolingual setting, where the entire execution process, including reasoning, tool invocation, and output generation, is conducted within a single language. In contrast, real-world applications often involve multilingual inputs and outputs within a unified workflow, yet the interaction between multilinguality and agentic execution remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce PolyWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on multilingual long-horizon workplace workflows. PolyWorkBench consists of 67 tasks across five domains, including commerce, knowledge work, legal analysis, localization, and manufacturing, where agents must process heterogeneous multilingual inputs, perform iterative reasoning, invoke external tools, and produce structured outputs. To enable comprehensive evaluation, we propose a hybrid framework that combines structural grading, executable verification, and LLM-based semantic assessment. This design allows us to capture both functional correctness and linguistic consistency across complex workflows. Empirical results show that state-of-the-art LLM agents suffer significant performance degradation in multilingual workflow settings compared to monolingual counterparts. Our analysis suggests that multilinguality introduces compounding effects across reasoning and execution steps, highlighting the importance of jointly modeling language variation and procedural decision-making in agent evaluation.

AI.tldr: A multilingual long-horizon workflow benchmark for evaluating LLM agents, PolyWorkBench, showing multilingual inputs/outputs across domains; a hybrid evaluation framework is proposed; results indicate multilinguality reduces agent performance and interacts with reasoning/execution steps.
AI.motivation: Bridge the gap in multilingual agent evaluation by introducing workflows that require multilingual processing, tool use, and structured outputs, reflecting real-world multilingual scenarios beyond monolingual benchmarks.
AI.method: Introduce PolyWorkBench with 67 tasks across five domains (commerce, knowledge work, legal analysis, localization, manufacturing). Tasks require heterogeneous multilingual inputs, iterative reasoning, tool invocation, and structured outputs. Use a hybrid evaluation framework combining structural grading, executable verification, and LLM-based semantic assessment to capture functional and linguistic performance.
AI.result: State-of-the-art LLM agents show significant performance degradation in multilingual workflow settings compared with monolingual benchmarks; multilinguality causes compounding effects across reasoning and execution steps.
AI.conclusion: Joint modeling of language variation and procedural decision-making is essential for robust agent evaluation; future work should address how multilinguality interacts with planning, tool use, and output generation in agent systems.

title: APVI-SLAM: Real-Time Acoustic-Pressure-Visual-Inertial Localization and Photorealistic Mapping System in Complex Underwater Environment
summary: Extreme subsea environments often cause severe feature de-gradation and estimator divergence in underwater visual-inertial SLAM. Although sensors like Doppler Velocity Logs (DVL) and pressure gauges provide auxiliary constraints, robust multi-sensor fusion during intermittent visual failure remains challenging. To address this, we present APVI-SLAM, a real-time multi-sensor fusion SLAM system that achieves both accurate underwater localization and photorealistic mapping. Our approach introduces a reliability-aware localization framework that dynamically reweights sensor estimators and employs a sliding-window freezing strategy to recover from tracking failures, substantially enhancing system robustness. Furthermore, for high-fidelity scenes reconstruction, we propose an efficient quadtree-guided mapping module that facilitates incremental water-medium modeling and 3D Gaussian optimization. Recognizing the lack of benchmark for underwater mapping evaluation, we also contribute a coral reef surveying dataset with synchronized multi-modality data. Extensive experiments on public and our proposed benchmarks demonstrate that APVI-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art localization and reconstruction quality at real-time speeds.

AI.tldr: APVI-SLAM is a real-time multi-sensor underwater SLAM system that achieves both accurate localization and photorealistic mapping through reliability-aware sensor fusion, a sliding-window freezing recovery strategy, and a quadtree-guided mapping with 3D Gaussian optimization, validated on coral reef data.
AI.motivation: Extreme subsea environments degrade visual features and cause estimator divergence; while DVL and pressure sensors provide auxiliary constraints, robust multi-sensor fusion during intermittent visual failure remains challenging.
AI.method: A reliability-aware localization framework wherein sensor estimators are dynamically reweighted; a sliding-window freezing strategy to recover from tracking failures; a quadtree-guided mapping module for incremental water-medium modeling; 3D Gaussian optimization; and a coral reef surveying dataset with synchronized multi-modality data.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and the authors’ dataset show that APVI-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art localization and reconstruction quality at real-time speeds.
AI.conclusion: APVI-SLAM advances robust underwater SLAM by combining adaptive sensor fusion, failure-recovery strategies, and efficient water-volume mapping, and provides a new benchmark dataset for underwater mapping evaluation.

title: Domain-Adaptive Climate Downscaling Under Temporal Distribution Shift
summary: Deep-learning-based climate downscaling aims to learn relationships from historical low-resolution (LR) and high-resolution (HR) climate data to generate HR climate projections. However, this setting faces a temporal out-of-distribution (OOD) challenge: models trained on historical data are commonly applied to future projections whose distributions may differ substantially from the training period. This study investigates temporal OOD shift for daily temperature downscaling over the Continental United States using paired LR-HR model simulations. We propose a temporal domain-adaptive downscaling framework that combines supervised HR reconstruction on historical data with domain alignment between historical and future climate distributions. Experiments across future validation periods show that the proposed domain-adaptive model consistently outperforms statistical and deep-learning-based bias-correction methods, with the largest gains occurring when the temporal distribution shift is strongest. Spatial analyses indicate stronger improvements over high-elevation and topographically complex regions, along with higher spatiotemporal correlation with the HR target. The extreme analysis shows that domain adaptation also reduces upper-tail temperature bias relative to the non-adaptive model. These results demonstrate that temporal domain adaptation can improve the robustness of HR climate projections under non-stationary climate conditions.

AI.tldr: Temporal domain-adaptive downscaling improves robustness of HR climate projections under non-stationary (temporal OOD) conditions by aligning historical and future distributions and performing supervised HR reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Address temporal distribution shift (OOD) when applying DL-based climate downscaling trained on historical data to future projections.
AI.method: Proposed temporal domain-adaptive downscaling framework combining supervised HR reconstruction on historical data with domain alignment between historical and future climate distributions.
AI.result: Outperforms statistical and DL-based bias-correction methods across future validation periods; largest gains under strong temporal shift; spatially stronger improvements over high-elevation/topographically complex regions; higher spatiotemporal correlation with HR target; reduces upper-tail temperature bias.
AI.conclusion: Temporal domain adaptation enhances robustness of high-resolution climate projections under non-stationary climate conditions.

title: ARMS: Anchor-Relational Motion Streaming for Seamless Solo-Social Motion Transitions
comment: Accepted by ECCV 2026. Project page: https://hkliu.com/arms
summary: Generating temporally continuous and socially coherent human motion from text remains a fundamental challenge, particularly in realistic streams where people act alone, enter interactions, and later disengage. Most existing methods generate fixed-length motion clips under static agent configurations, which makes them brittle to solo-social transitions and unsuitable for incremental generation over long horizons. We propose ARMS, an Anchor-Relational Motion Streaming framework that unifies solo motion and human-human interaction within a single causal generative process. ARMS introduces a dynamics-asymmetric representation that decouples per-person temporal evolution from inter-person alignment via a partner-referenced relative-translation term, enabling seamless switching of social coupling without sacrificing long-horizon stability or spatial consistency between agents. On top of a causal latent space, a causal relational diffusion model progressively refines motion segment by segment using only past context, capturing both intra-person temporal dependencies and inter-person relations. Mode-aware relational gating activates or masks cross-agent connections, allowing the same model to support both solo and interaction generation. Experiments show that ARMS improves transition smoothness and social coherence compared to interaction-centric baselines, while also achieving competitive results on human-human interaction benchmarks.

AI.tldr: ARMS unifies solo and social motion streaming with a dynamics-asymmetric representation and causal relational diffusion; supports long-horizon, incremental generation and mode-aware gating.
AI.motivation: To address brittle fixed-length clips and poor long-horizon, seamless solo-to-social transitions in motion generation by unifying solo and interaction in a single causal process.
AI.method: Proposes ARMS: Anchor-Relational Motion Streaming; decouples per-person temporal evolution from inter-person alignment via a partner-referenced relative-translation term; uses a causal latent space and a causal relational diffusion model; employs mode-aware relational gating to switch between solo and interaction; refines motion segment-by-segment using past context.
AI.result: Empirical improvements in transition smoothness and social coherence over interaction-centric baselines; competitive results on human-human interaction benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: ARMS yields stable, spatially consistent long-horizon motion generation with seamless transitions and scalable streaming for both solo and social scenarios.

title: Reward-Density Heuristic for Dynamic Multi-Vehicle Routing: Performance and Computational Efficiency
summary: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) and its variants represent some of the most practically consequential optimization challenges in modern logistics and urban mobility. In this study, we address a dynamic, online variant combining elements of the VRP and the Orienteering Problem (OP), in which a fleet of vehicles must maximise cumulative reward collected within a fixed time horizon while continuously replanning as new tasks arrive. We propose and evaluate a reward-density heuristic for dynamic multi-vehicle assignment, referred to as the Efficiency heuristic. We evaluate this formulation across two application domains: autonomous drone task allocation and urban taxi dispatch, across multiple fleet sizes and task scales. The proposed method is compared with four classical construction heuristics and three metaheuristic algorithms (Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search, Genetic Algorithm, and Simulated Annealing), all evaluated under identical conditions. Across all tested configurations, the Efficiency heuristic matches the solution quality of the best metaheuristic algorithms while requiring two to three orders of magnitude less planning time, establishing Pareto dominance over all competing methods on the reward-versus-compute frontier. These findings suggest a practical design principle for real-time allocation and dispatch systems: in dynamic, time-constrained routing environments, carefully designed greedy heuristics can match the output of sophisticated search procedures at a fraction of the computational cost, making them preferable for online deployment.

AI.tldr: Dynamic VRP/OP problem; proposes Efficiency reward-density heuristic for online multi-vehicle assignment; achieves solution quality similar to metaheuristics but with 2–3 orders of magnitude faster planning, yielding Pareto dominance on reward vs compute; supports use of greedy heuristics for real-time allocation.
AI.motivation: Need to solve dynamic, time-constrained routing where tasks arrive online; combine VRP and OP; maximize cumulative reward within fixed horizon with replanning.
AI.method: Introduce Efficiency heuristic based on reward density for dynamic multi-vehicle assignment; compare against four construction heuristics and three metaheuristics (Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search, Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing) under identical conditions; evaluate in drone and taxi domains across fleet sizes and task scales.
AI.result: Efficiency heuristic matches best metaheuristics in solution quality, while dramatically reducing planning time (2–3 orders of magnitude); demonstrates Pareto dominance on reward–compute frontier.
AI.conclusion: Greedy, well-designed heuristics can match sophisticated search methods in real-time dynamic routing; recommended for online deployment; design principle for time-constrained systems.

title: RoboVAST: Automated Scenario-Based Validation of Robots at Scale
summary: Validation of robotic systems critically depends on the operating conditions under which they are assessed. Scenario selection and variation are often manual, experience-driven, and difficult to scale, which harms reproducibility and weakens validation conclusions. We propose a scenario-based methodology that models scenarios compositionally and formalizes how these dimensions are varied, instantiated, executed, and interpreted. Building on this, we introduce RoboVAST, a framework that realizes declarative campaign specifications, plugin-based scenario generation, and scalable containerized execution with integrated result analysis. We demonstrate the approach with a navigation dataset comprising 5480 scenario configurations and over 100000 execution runs across five indoor maps with varied paths, sensor noise, software parameters, and obstacle settings, totaling more than 1800 hours of simulated operation and 1873 km traveled. Twenty repetitions per configuration allow us to distinguish systematic failures from stochastic anomalies.

AI.tldr: A compositional, scalable scenario-based validation framework (RoboVAST) that declaratively defines campaigns, generates scenarios via plugins, runs them in containers, and analyzes results; demonstrated on a navigation dataset with 5480 configurations, 100k+ runs, five maps, extensive variation, and 20 repeats per config to separate systematic failures from stochastic noise.
AI.motivation: To improve reproducibility and scalability in robotic system validation by moving from manual, experience-driven scenario selection to a compositional, formalized approach that can scale across many scenarios and runs.
AI.method: Propose a compositional model of scenarios, declarative campaign specifications, plugin-based scenario generation, and scalable containerized execution with integrated result analysis (RoboVAST). Demonstrate via a navigation dataset with thousands of configurations, large numbers of runs across multiple maps, with varied paths, sensor noise, software parameters, and obstacles; include multiple repetitions per configuration to distinguish systematic issues from stochastic variation.
AI.result: Empirical demonstration on a navigation dataset: 5 indoor maps, 5480 scenario configurations, over 100000 execution runs, more than 1800 hours of simulated operation, and 1873 km traveled; 20 repetitions per configuration enable separation of systematic failures from stochastic anomalies.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables reproducible, scalable validation of robotic systems by formalizing scenario variation and providing declarative campaigns, plugin-based generation, and containerized execution with integrated analysis; the large-scale run data supports robust identification of failures and performance trends.

title: Orthogonal Dendritic Intrinsic Networks: An Architecture for Significance-Ordered, Orthogonal Latent Spaces
summary: Principal Component Analysis or PCA-like properties (orthogonality, variance ranking) are seldom realized in deep autoencoder architectures. In this work, we present ODIN (Orthogonal Dendritic Intrinsic Network), a novel autoencoder architecture that recovers PCA-like latent structure in a fully non-linear regime. By incorporating a set of geometric constraints directly into the training objective, ODIN encourages latent dimensions to be mutually orthogonal and ordered by explained variance, mirroring the interpretable decomposition of PCA while retaining the expressive power of deep networks. We provide theoretical grounding for these constraints and demonstrate their compatibility with standard encoder-decoder frameworks. We also establish empirical results for both synthetic and real world datasets, establishing a principled path toward interpretable, structured feature learning and dimensionality reduction.

AI.tldr: ODIN enforces PCA-like latent structure in a nonlinear autoencoder by adding geometric constraints that enforce orthogonality and explained-variance ordering; supports interpretable dimensionality reduction with theoretical grounding and empirical validation.
AI.motivation: PCA-like interpretability is rarely realized in deep autoencoders; there is a need for latent factors that are mutually orthogonal and ranked by explained variance in nonlinear deep models.
AI.method: Introduce geometric constraints into the training objective to enforce latent orthogonality and variance ranking; demonstrate compatibility with standard encoder–decoder architectures; provide theoretical justification and formal analysis; validate on synthetic and real-world datasets.
AI.result: Provides theoretical grounding and empirical evidence that PCA-like latent structure can emerge in a nonlinear autoencoder (ODIN), enabling interpretable and structured feature learning and effective dimensionality reduction.
AI.conclusion: ODIN offers a principled framework to reconcile PCA-like properties with deep nonlinear representations, enabling interpretable, structured latent factors and guiding future work on interpretable dimensionality reduction in neural networks.

title: Optimized Adaptive Loop Filter in Versatile Video Coding
comment: This paper was submitted to DCC 2021 and accepted as a poster
summary: In the Versatile Video Coding~(VVC) standard, adaptive loop filter~(ALF), including Geometry transformation-based Adaptive Loop Filter~(GALF) and Cross Component Adaptive Loop Filter~(CCALF), plays an essential role in reducing compression artifacts. However, it also has high coding complexity and requires many picture buffer accesses in the encoder that will increase external memory access and is unfriendly to the software and hardware design. Therefore, we propose an optimized ALF framework, including the parallel design of GALF and CCALF, the adaptive parameter decision of GALF, and one-pass CCALF scheme by effectively estimating the CCALF filtering distortion without conducting filter operation. Compared to VTM-8.0, the proposed method can reduce the picture buffer access from 152 to 1 and achieve roughly 25\% time-savings of the ALF module with negligible coding performance change under RA configuration. Some of the proposed methods have been adopted in the VVC reference software.

AI.tldr: An optimized ALF framework for VVC that dramatically reduces memory access and computation with minimal RD impact.
AI.motivation: ALF in VVC (GALF and CCALF) provides artifact suppression but incurs high coding complexity and large picture buffer accesses, hindering software/hardware efficiency.
AI.method: Introduce an optimized ALF framework featuring (1) parallel design of GALF and CCALF, (2) adaptive parameter decision for GALF, and (3) a one-pass CCALF scheme that estimates filtering distortion without performing the filter.
AI.result: Compared with VTM-8.0, picture buffer access drops from 152 to 1 and ALF module time is reduced by ~25% with negligible RD change under RA configuration; some proposals have been adopted in the VVC reference software.
AI.conclusion: The proposed optimizations significantly reduce memory access and computational burden of ALF while maintaining RD performance, and demonstrate practical viability through adoption in reference software.

title: When do prophets profit in prediction markets?
summary: Prediction markets aggregate dispersed beliefs into prices that act as probabilistic forecasts of uncertain events. Classical theory establishes a clean equivalence between forecasting accuracy and trading profit, but only for the specific automated market maker (AMM) design. However, the largest exchanges today are based on central limit order books in which informed forecasters routinely lose money while uninformed strategies can profit on simple heuristics. We resolve this discrepancy by establishing a formal equivalence between predictive accuracy and profitability. For any strictly proper scoring rule $S$, we exhibit a "proper" betting strategy that depends only on the forecaster's prediction $\mathbf{p}$ and the market price $\mathbf{q}$, and earns positive expected profit whenever $\mathbf{p}$ outperforms $\mathbf{q}$ under $S$ and the market has sufficient liquidity. Moreover, this proper betting is essentially the only strategy with such robust profitability guarantee. The proof rests on a decomposition of expected profit that strictly generalizes the classical AMM guarantee and also explains how strategies can profit without an accuracy edge. Empirically, across thousands of forecasts by AI models, proper betting is the only strategy that reliably converts accuracy into profit, and we further identify systematic forecasting personas and show how the optimal proper strategy varies across them. A month-long live deployment on Kalshi achieves $+80.33\%$ return on investment with a Sharpe ratio of $3.35$.

AI.tldr: A general equivalence is established between forecast accuracy and profitability for prediction markets beyond AMMs, via a unique proper betting strategy aligned with any strictly proper scoring rule S. This strategy, depending only on the forecaster’s prediction p and market price q, ensures positive expected profit when p outperforms q under S in sufficiently liquid markets; it uniquely characterizes profitability guarantees and explains profits even without an accuracy edge. Empirical validation across AI forecasts shows proper betting as the sole reliable converter of accuracy into profit; live deployment on Kalshi yielded +80.33% ROI and Sharpe 3.35.
AI.motivation: Classical results tie accuracy and trading profit only for automated market makers, while real-world central limit order books show profits for uninformed heuristics and losses for informed forecasters. The work seeks a formal, robust link between predictive accuracy and profitability that applies to general market designs and explains when and how forecasting skills translate to profits.
AI.method: Define a family of proper betting strategies derived from any strictly proper scoring rule S. Prove that a strategy depending only on p and q earns positive expected profit whenever p outruns q under S, given market liquidity. Decompose expected profit to generalize the AMM guarantee and isolate conditions under which profitability can occur absent accuracy edges. Prove uniqueness of the robust profitable strategy. Empirically evaluate across thousands of AI forecasts and analyze forecasting personas; implement a month-long live test on Kalshi.
AI.result: The proper betting strategy yields positive expected profit when p outperforms q under S, robust to liquidity within reasonable bounds. It is essentially the only strategy with such a universal profitability guarantee. Empirical results show proper betting uniquely converts accuracy to profit across diverse forecasts; live deployment on Kalshi achieved +80.33% ROI and Sharpe ratio of 3.35.
AI.conclusion: A formal, general equivalence between predictive accuracy and profitability is established for general market designs, extending AMM guarantees and clarifying why profits can occur without accuracy edges. The approach informs market design, forecaster strategy, and risk management, and identifies forecasting personas with optimal strategies varying by persona.

title: Diagnosing Semantic Handoff Failures in Agent-Orchestrated Vision-Language-Action Skill Composition
summary: Long-horizon household tasks require robots to compose many language-conditioned skills, yet the boundary between consecutive skills is rarely explicit. A skill may satisfy its own postcondition while leaving the robot, objects, or camera views in a state from which the next skill cannot reliably start. We study this semantic handoff problem in BEHAVIOR-1K through an agent-orchestrated vision-language-action execution harness. The harness invokes $π_{0.5}$-based skill checkpoints trained from cleaned BEHAVIOR-1K demonstrations, assigns each skill typed arguments and a step budget, and uses multi-view vision-language model verification to decide whether execution should advance, retry, or replan. To separate isolated skill competence from long-horizon compositional robustness, we evaluate the same checkpoints under two initial-state distributions: clean skill-boundary snapshots and chained terminal states produced by previous skills. Selected navigation, grasping, placement, and door-opening skills achieve 77--100% success from clean snapshots under human-reviewed verification, yet composed rollouts still frequently stall from chained states. Execution traces attribute these failures to next-skill readiness, target grounding, and low-level control execution, revealing a substantial gap between single-skill success and reliable long-horizon task completion. These findings turn near-zero end-to-end task success into actionable diagnostics, showing that future VLA skill libraries must learn robustness to the messy chained-state distribution that clean demonstrations systematically underrepresent.

AI.tldr: High-level: The work studies semantic handoffs in long-horizon robot tasks using BEHAVIOR-1K skill checkpoints and a vision-language-action (VLA) harness. It reveals strong single-skill performance under clean conditions but a large drop in end-to-end success when chained-state distributions are present, highlighting robustness gaps and the need for VLA libraries to handle messy state transitions.
AI.motivation: Address the boundary problem between consecutive, conditioned skills in long-horizon robotic tasks. Demonstrate how skill libraries trained on clean demonstrations fail to generalize to the chained states that occur during end-to-end execution, and propose diagnostics via a VLM-verification harness.
AI.method: Train π_{0.5}-based skill checkpoints from BEHAVIOR-1K; assign typed arguments and step budgets; use multi-view vision-language model verification to decide whether to advance, retry, or replan. Evaluate two initial-state distributions: clean skill-boundary snapshots and chained terminal states produced by previous skills. Test navigation, grasping, placement, and door-opening skills; report success under human-reviewed verification.
AI.result: Selected skills achieve 77–100% success from clean snapshots under verification. However, when rolled out end-to-end with chained states, performance stalls frequently. Failures are attributed to next-skill readiness, target grounding, and low-level control, indicating a substantial gap between single-skill success and reliable long-horizon completion.
AI.conclusion: Future VLA skill libraries must learn robustness to messy chained-state distributions that clean demonstrations underrepresent. The work provides actionable diagnostics to guide development toward more robust long-horizon, language-conditioned robotic execution.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Battery Management of Autonomous Order Pickers
summary: Battery charging of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) in warehouses is a critical operational challenge that heavily impacts both order processing times and throughput. In this study, we address the dynamic AMR charging problem under stochastic order arrivals, where robots must learn optimal charging decisions. Traditional fixed-rule heuristics often prove suboptimal in dynamic environments and fail to account for multi-AMR coordination, leading to severe resource inefficiencies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework designed for multi-block warehouses with fixed charging stations. Our model dynamically learns two key decisions: charging station selection and optimal charging duration, explicitly accounting for anticipated queuing times at the stations. Extensive numerical experiments benchmark the proposed model against state-of-the-art DRL and traditional heuristic approaches. Results demonstrate that our PPO framework increases order-completion rates by up to 6\% compared to the strongest baseline, while significantly reducing the total time dedicated to recharging operations. Furthermore, we validate the model's robustness across diverse warehouse configurations and stochastic arrival rates. Finally, we interpret the learned DRL policy, offering valuable operational insights into its superiority over standard benchmarks.

AI.tldr: PPO-based DRL for multi-robot charging in warehouses; learns station choice and charging duration to minimize queue delays and boost order throughput, outperforming baselines by up to 6%.
AI.motivation: Dynamic charging for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) under stochastic order arrivals; fixed heuristics fail to coordinate multiple robots and charging queues, causing inefficiencies.
AI.method: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) based deep reinforcement learning framework for multi-block warehouses with fixed charging stations. The model outputs two actions: charging station selection and charging duration, incorporating anticipated station queuing. Training is conducted in a simulated stochastic arrival environment and benchmarked against state-of-the-art DRL and heuristic baselines.
AI.result: The approach increases order-completion rates by up to 6% over the strongest baseline and reduces total recharging time. It shows robustness across various warehouse configurations and arrival rates; the learned policy offers interpretability and operational insights.
AI.conclusion: A PPO-based DRL framework effectively coordinates AMR charging in multi-block warehouses with fixed stations, improving throughput and reducing recharge-related time; the method demonstrates robust performance and practical insights for deployment.

title: Image2Sim: Scaling Embodied Navigation via Generative Neural Simulator
summary: Embodied navigation aims to build agents that interpret multimodal goals, reason in 3D space, and reach target destinations reliably in the real world. However, progress remains constrained by the lack of scalable, high-fidelity, and physically grounded interactive environments. Although real-world scanned datasets offer visual realism, they are limited by scale. In contrast, synthetic simulators scale more easily but often exhibit large sim-to-real gaps. We introduce Image2Sim, a real-time neural simulation framework that constructs high-quality interactive environments from posed RGB-D image sequences. The central idea is to decouple 3D spatial anchoring from photorealistic observation synthesis. For scene construction, Image2Sim uses a feed-forward feature Gaussian model that lifts posed RGB-D observations into a 3D feature-Gaussian representation in a single pass. For rendering, we propose a Geometry-Aware One-Step Pixel Flow model that transforms sparse and noisy Gaussian projections into high-quality panoramic RGB-D observations. Image2Sim also serves as a fully automated embodied data engine that generates high-fidelity observations, executable actions, and diverse navigation instructions at scale. It converts large collections of videos and images into nearly 20K interactive scenes and synthesizes more than 10 million navigation training samples. Navigation models trained entirely in these neural environments achieve strong improvements on major benchmarks and transfer effectively to real-world zero-shot settings. These results suggest that scalable neural simulation can serve as a practical training substrate for embodied navigation at scale.

AI.tldr: Image2Sim introduces a real-time neural simulation framework that builds interactive 3D scenes from posed RGB-D data by decoupling 3D spatial anchoring from photorealistic observation synthesis, enabling scalable embodied navigation training with strong zero-shot transfer to real-world settings.
AI.motivation: Overcome the scale and realism gap in embodied navigation: real-world scanned datasets are realistic but small in scale, while synthetic simulators scale poorly in realism; a scalable, high-fidelity neural simulator could bridge this gap.
AI.method: 1) A feed-forward feature-Gaussian model lifts posed RGB-D observations into a 3D feature-Gaussian representation for scene construction. 2) A Geometry-Aware One-Step Pixel Flow rendering model converts sparse, noisy Gaussian projections into high-quality panoramic RGB-D observations. 3) An automated data engine generates observations, executable actions, and diverse navigation instructions, producing ~20k interactive scenes and over 10M navigation samples.
AI.result: Navigation models trained in these neural environments achieve strong improvements on major benchmarks and transfer effectively to real-world zero-shot settings.
AI.conclusion: Scalable neural simulation can serve as a practical training substrate for embodied navigation at scale.

title: A toy framework for single and multi-agent human-AI curiosity ecosystems
summary: This paper offers a toy framework for considering curiosity as an ecosystem. First, it suggests that a single agent's inquiry policy (how, when, and why an agent asks a question) depends on how the agent values immediate uncertainty reduction, costs, delayed return, and the value of keeping the question open. A key concept in the framework is that the weights on these decision-related terms can change with experience. For example, a period of cheap, quickly answered questions may change the cost of inquiry on a short timescale and change which kinds of questions the agent is drawn to answer over a longer timescale. Second, these ideas are extended to many agents exploring a shared knowledge landscape, and there the framework tracks inquiry volume, topic diversity, frontier-directed inquiry, redundancy, and reusable knowledge. The result is a conceptual toy framework for studying curiosity ecology and for future efforts towards designing multi-agent AI systems for discovery. It serves as a companion piece for a paper currently under review in Trends in Neurosciences.

AI.tldr: Toy theoretical framework for curiosity as an ecosystem, where an agent’s inquiry policy is governed by trade-offs among immediate uncertainty reduction, cost, delayed return, and keeping questions open; weights on these terms evolve with experience and differ in a multi-agent setting, affecting inquiry volume, topic diversity, frontier exploration, redundancy, and reusable knowledge. Serves as a scaffolding for studying curiosity ecology and guiding multi-agent discovery AI; companion to neuroscience work.
AI.motivation: To formalize curiosity as a dynamic, experience-dependent ecosystem that shapes both individual and collective inquiry, enabling principled analysis and design of curiosity-driven AI for discovery.
AI.method: Conceptual/theoretical model (a toy framework) that parameterizes inquiry decisions via time-varying weights on decision terms (uncertainty reduction, costs, delayed return, keeping question open) and extends the framework to multiple agents exploring a shared knowledge landscape, with metrics like volume, diversity, frontier-directed inquiry, redundancy, and reuse of knowledge.
AI.result: Provides a conceptual scaffolding for curiosity ecology; clarifies how inquiry and its drivers evolve across short and long timescales and across agents. Positioned as a companion piece to a neuroscience-review paper; no empirical validation within the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Offers a tractable, high-level foundation for studying curiosity ecology and guiding the design of multi-agent discovery systems; substantial empirical and operational work needed to formalize, validate, and implement these ideas in AI systems.

title: Optimal Transport Q-Learning for Flow Policy Steering and Acceleration
summary: Diffusion and flow policies have recently demonstrated remarkable performance in robotic applications by accurately capturing multimodal robot trajectory distributions, especially in the context of vision language action (VLA) models. However, high quality policy performance also requires fast inference and high quality demonstrations, which are often hard to get. Lack of these leads to suboptimal policy behaviors and failure under distribution shifts. In this work we address the problem of fine-tuning and accelerating suboptimal flow-based policies using the robot's experience through RL post-training. We introduce Optimal Transport Q-Learning (OTQL), a new method for finetuning flow policies using advantage weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching. OTQL can finetune and accelerate flows with an interaction budget of 50-60 episodes while avoiding computationally expensive distillation in simulation and real-world robot tasks. Our results show that OTQL post-trains flow policies using the robot's own experience, increasing average success percentage of single-task policies from 36% to 86% and of a pre-trained VLA from 38% to 76% while reducing the number of inference steps per action generation by 70%.

AI.tldr: Introduces OTQL, a post-training RL method that fine-tunes and accelerates suboptimal flow-based policies via advantage-weighted optimal transport flow matching, using the robot’s own experience with ~50–60 episodes, achieving large gains in success rates and substantial inference-time reductions without distillation.
AI.motivation: To overcome suboptimal performance due to limited/high-quality demonstrations and distribution shifts in diffusion/flow policies for robotic tasks, while also ensuring fast inference and practicality of training.
AI.method: Proposes Optimal Transport Q-Learning (OTQL) that performs advantage-weighted conditional optimal transport flow matching to fine-tune flow policies. It uses RL post-training with an interaction budget (~50–60 episodes) and avoids computationally expensive distillation in simulation or real robots.
AI.result: Empirical gains include increasing single-task policy success from 36% to 86% and a pre-trained VLA from 38% to 76%; inference steps per action reduced by ~70%. OTQL learns from the robot’s own experience rather than relying on expert demonstrations.
AI.conclusion: OTQL enables effective, data-efficient post-training refinement of flow-based policies, improving performance under distribution shifts and reducing inference cost without distillation.

title: LLM-Driven Neural Network Generation with Same-Family Architecture Guidance: Disentangling Transfer and Adaptation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate neural-network modifications, but unrestricted generation is often invalid or harmful. This paper studies a narrower setting: improving a weak target model using a stronger same-family source model from a neural-network database. We propose a source-guided candidate-generation protocol with non-source controls, source-conditioned candidates, and a no-LLM hp_copy ablation under equal evaluation budgets. The protocol reports validity separately from accuracy and selects the best valid candidate only when it improves the target. On CIFAR-10, the strongest source-guided candidate reaches 0.5049 accuracy versus 0.2398 for the best non-source candidate, a +0.2651 advantage, while improving a weak target originally at 0.1254; a five-epoch check preserves the gain at 0.7686 versus 0.4839. On SVHN AlexNet with DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, source-guided transfer reaches 0.7880 versus 0.2254, a +0.5626 advantage; a fresh repeat reaches 0.8069 versus 0.2509, a +0.5560 advantage. Direct source-recipe copy produces 0.1959 on SVHN AlexNet, matching the original target, while hp_transfer reaches 0.7880, showing that the LLM adapts rather than copies the source recipe. Family-level analysis shows the clearest positive signals for AlexNet, with 6/8 wins across SVHN, Imagenette, and CelebA-Gender, and alt_nn1, with 8/10 wins on CIFAR-10.

AI.tldr: Source-guided candidate generation using a stronger same-family model improves weak targets while enforcing validity; demonstrates significant gains on CIFAR-10 and SVHN with AlexNet and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B; LLM adapts rather than copying source recipes.
AI.motivation: Unrestricted LLM-generated neural-network modifications risk invalid or harmful changes. Investigate a constrained protocol that leverages stronger same-family source models from a neural-network database to improve a weak target under budgeted evaluation, with explicit validity checks.
AI.method: Source-guided candidate-generation protocol with non-source controls, source-conditioned candidates, and a no-LLM hp_copy ablation under equal evaluation budgets. Report validity separately from accuracy; select the best valid candidate only if it improves the target. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and SVHN with AlexNet, using DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B as the source-model family; comparisons include direct source-copy, hp_transfer, and multiple repeats; five-epoch checks for stability; family-level analysis across architectures and datasets.
AI.result: Strong improvements: CIFAR-10—best source-guided candidate: 0.5049 vs 0.2398 (non-source), +0.2651; target originally 0.1254 improves to 0.4839; five-epoch check preserves the gain with the target at 0.7686 vs 0.4839. SVHN AlexNet with DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B—source-guided transfer: 0.7880 vs 0.2254 (+0.5626); fresh repeat: 0.8069 vs 0.2509 (+0.5560). Direct source-copy yields 0.1959 on SVHN AlexNet (matching the original target), while hp_transfer reaches 0.7880, indicating adaptation rather than copying the source recipe. Family-level: AlexNet shows 6/8 wins across SVHN, Imagenette, CelebA-Gender; alt_nn1 shows 8/10 wins on CIFAR-10.
AI.conclusion: The protocol yields robust, statistically meaningful improvements by leveraging stronger same-family source models under controlled validity checks, with evidence that the LLM adapts rather than merely copying source recipes. Gains are observed across multiple datasets and architectures, suggesting broad applicability within the same model family.

title: LEGATO 2: Toward Multimodal Sheet Music Recognition and Understanding
