Key analysis shows: (1) promotion separates interfaces; (2) replacement preserves feasibility under an interface-slack condition; (3) graph construction is invariant to row-column permutations.
AI.result: Empirical MILP generation using GraphBU yields graph-statistical similarity to the source around 0.934, feasibility around 96.7%, and about 8.0% average improvement in the main PS index on downstream training.
AI.conclusion: GraphBU provides a graph-native, interface-aware unit for MILP instance generation that preserves structural characteristics, maintains high feasibility, and enhances downstream Learn-to-Search pipelines, with permutation invariance guaranteeing robustness to row/column ordering.

title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
summary: Reliable seam segmentation is essential for autonomous robotic welding in construction, where harsh illumination, specular reflections, and thin weld geometries often degrade segmentation performance. This study proposes a reflection-robust seam segmentation framework that enhances a BiSeNetV2 backbone through transfer learning and a hybrid Cross-Entropy--Lovász loss. Rather than increasing architectural complexity, the proposed framework improves reflection robustness through learning-stability-oriented optimization. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 81.76\% Joint IoU and 90.73\% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by +22.36 percentage points over the OHEM-based baseline while maintaining identical FLOPs, parameter count, and inference speed. The proposed approach also recovers 96.33\% of severe zero-IoU failure cases under reflective conditions. Comparative experiments across BiSeNetV2, DeepLabV3+, UNet, and SegFormer further demonstrate that the proposed optimization strategy is particularly effective for lightweight real-time segmentation architectures. Qualitative analyses additionally show improved seam continuity and reflection robustness in challenging welding environments. These findings suggest that the proposed framework provides a practical and lightweight perception solution for robotic welding applications involving reflective metallic surfaces.

AI.tldr: A lightweight, transfer-learning–driven seam segmentation method robust to reflections, built on BiSeNetV2 with a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász loss, achieving substantial Joint IoU gains without extra FLOPs and improving robustness against severe reflective conditions.
AI.motivation: Robust seam segmentation is essential for autonomous welding in harsh illumination and on reflective metals; existing methods struggle with reflections and thin weld geometries, and adding complexity is undesirable for real-time robotics.
AI.method: Enhance a BiSeNetV2 backbone via transfer learning and a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász loss, with a learning-stability–oriented optimization that avoids increasing architectural complexity.
AI.result: 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU; +22.36 percentage points Joint IoU over an OHEM-based baseline; identical FLOPs, parameter count, and inference speed; recovers 96.33% of severe zero-IoU failures under reflective conditions; effective across multiple lightweight segmentation backbones.
AI.conclusion: The framework offers a practical, lightweight solution for reflective-surface seam segmentation in robotic welding, particularly beneficial for real-time, resource-constrained architectures.

title: Graph Convolutional Attention: A Spectral Perspective on Graph Denoising and Diffusion
summary: Denoising graphs is a fundamental problem in graph learning and the core operation of graph diffusion models. Attention-based architectures like graph transformers have recently shown promise in denoising graphs. However, our principled understanding of attention-based graph denoising remains limited, making it unclear whether standard attention is the right mechanism for this task. Here we show that, under a denoising objective, linear attention is suboptimal and can only learn an average spectral denoising filter over the training distribution. This creates a fundamental limitation as graphs often vary spectrally across the distribution. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Spectral Attention, which directly utilizes the input graph spectrum and provably outperforms linear attention by a margin governed by the spectral diversity of the distribution. We then derive Graph Convolutional Attention (GCA), a practical and permutation-equivariant realization of this idea that implements spectral denoising through graph-filtered queries and keys. For stochastic block models, GCA provably matches the idealized Spectral Attention mechanism. We further show that the softmax operation, that follows the attention, provides additional denoising by approximately projecting noisy eigenvectors onto the clean eigenspace. Empirically, replacing linear attention with GCA consistently improves graph denoising and diffusion on synthetic and real datasets, with gains strongly correlated with spectral diversity. In DiGress, GCA matches standard graph-transformer performance without computing expensive structural features, and when combined with the recently proposed PEARL positional encodings, avoids explicit eigendecomposition computations resulting in faster inference without degrading quality. The code can be found here: github.com/shervinkhalafi/graph_conv_att

AI.tldr: Linear attention is insufficient for graph denoising; propose Spectral Attention and Graph Convolutional Attention (GCA), leveraging input spectrum for improved denoising; theoretical and empirical gains, with efficient variants for large-scale graphs and diffusion models; code released.
AI.motivation: Understanding the limitations of attention in graph denoising and the need for mechanisms that adapt to spectral diversity across the data distribution; standard linear attention yields only an average spectral denoising effect and fails to capture spectral variability.
AI.method: Introduce Spectral Attention that uses the input graph spectrum; derive GCA as a permutation-equivariant, practical realization implementing spectral denoising via graph-filtered queries/keys; provide theoretical results on stochastic block models showing GCA matches ideal Spectral Attention; analyze the denoising effect of the post-attention softmax; conduct empirical evaluations on synthetic and real datasets, including DiGress with PEARL encodings to avoid eigendecomposition.
AI.result: GCA provably matches the ideal Spectral Attention on stochastic block models; softmax post-processing further denoises by projecting noisy eigenvectors to the clean eigenspace; empirical improvements in graph denoising/diffusion correlate with spectral diversity; DiGress with GCA achieves graph-transformer performance without costly structural features and with PEARL can avoid eigendecompositions, yielding faster inference without quality loss.
AI.conclusion: Spectral-based attention mechanisms outperform linear attention for graph denoising tasks; spectral diversity governs the magnitude of gains; the proposed GCA provides a practical, permutation-equivariant approach with theoretical guarantees and empirical benefits, and can enable faster inference in diffusion models.

title: High-Resolution Artwork Outpainting with Global Blueprint Guidance and Layout Control
summary: Image outpainting extends an image beyond its original borders, requiring seamless style integration and globally coherent scene completion. Building on the success of diffusion models, recent methods have achieved substantial improvements in visual quality. In practice, however, high-resolution outpainting is commonly performed via progressive expansion around a fixed source image, particularly in artwork scenarios. Despite this progress, existing approaches still suffer from three key limitations: (i) the absence of a reliable global planning mechanism, which leads to structural instability and error accumulation at high resolutions; (ii) limited spatial controllability beyond text prompts, making it difficult to place objects at user-specified locations; and (iii) high inference latency caused by inherently sequential patch generation. To address these issues, we propose a global blueprint-guided two-stage diffusion framework for layout-controllable high-resolution outpainting with efficient parallel synthesis. In Stage 1, we generate a low-resolution global blueprint using a layout adapter that injects bounding-box conditions into a Stable Diffusion inpainting backbone, producing a globally consistent structural plan while extracting global guidance features. In Stage 2, we synthesize high-resolution local patches in parallel by injecting the blueprint-derived global guidance and initializing each patch from the blueprint using the low-frequency preservation property of forward diffusion. This design eliminates sequential dependency while maintaining global coherence. Extensive experiments on large-scale artwork datasets demonstrate improved visual fidelity, stronger semantic consistency, and substantially reduced inference time compared to prior baselines, while uniquely supporting explicit layout control for artwork outpainting.

AI.tldr: A two-stage diffusion framework for high-resolution, layout-controllable image outpainting using a global blueprint. Stage 1 creates a low-res global blueprint via a layout-adapted inpainting backbone; Stage 2 performs parallel, high-res patch synthesis guided by the blueprint with low-frequency initialization.
AI.motivation: To overcome (i) lack of reliable global planning leading to instability at high res, (ii) limited spatial controllability beyond text prompts, and (iii) high latency from sequential patch generation in existing diffusion-based outpainting methods.
AI.method: Stage 1: Generate a low-resolution global blueprint by injecting bounding-box conditions into a Stable Diffusion inpainting backbone using a layout adapter, extracting global guidance features. Stage 2: Synthesize high-resolution local patches in parallel by injecting blueprint-derived guidance and initializing each patch from the blueprint using the low-frequency preservation property of forward diffusion, thereby removing sequential dependency while maintaining global coherence.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on large-scale artwork datasets show improved visual fidelity and semantic consistency, with substantially reduced inference time compared to prior baselines, and explicit support for layout-controlled artwork outpainting.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a global blueprint-guided, two-stage diffusion framework that addresses planning, controllability, and efficiency in high-resolution outpainting, enabling coherent global structure and faster inference with explicit layout control.

title: MobileWan: Closing the Quality Gap for Mobile Video Diffusion
summary: Recent advances in video diffusion have been driven by scaling transformer-based architectures to billions of parameters, substantially improving visual fidelity and motion coherence. In contrast, existing mobile video diffusion models remain limited to relatively small parameter budgets, typically 0.4-1.8B, restricting generation quality. In this work, we show that high-quality mobile video generation does not require small models. Instead, we demonstrate that a server-scale 5B-parameter video diffusion transformer can be deployed efficiently on memory-constrained mobile hardware through recurrent reformulation and structured compression. Starting from Wan2.2-5B, we rely on a recurrence distillation framework that converts video generation into a chunk-wise autoregressive process with constant-memory attention computation. Combined with causal linear attention, the model operates as an RNN at inference time while preserving temporal coherence across chunks. We further propose a learnable attention head pruning method based on binary per-head gates optimized end-to-end using a noise-biased sparsity objective and distillation-based finetuning. Together with sampling-step distillation and memory-optimized VAE decoding, MobileWan becomes the first 5B-scale video diffusion model deployable on a commercial mobile device. Our system generates 5-second 480x832 videos at 16 FPS in 20 seconds end-to-end latency, achieving a VBench score of 83.79 and establishing a new state of the art in mobile video generation. Project page: https://qualcomm-ai-research.github.io/mobilewan

AI.tldr: A 5B-parameter video diffusion transformer (MobileWan) deploys on mobile via recurrence distillation, structured pruning, and memory-optimized decoding, delivering 5s 480×832 video at 16 FPS with state-of-the-art mobile performance.
AI.motivation: Bridge the performance gap between server-scale diffusion models and memory-constrained mobile hardware by showing it is possible to run large models efficiently on-device without sacrificing quality or latency.
AI.method: Recurrence distillation converts video generation into a chunk-wise autoregressive process with constant-memory attention; uses causal linear attention to behave like an RNN at inference; introduces learnable per-head gate pruning with noise-biased sparsity objective and distillation-based fine-tuning; employs sampling-step distillation and memory-optimized VAE decoding; builds on Wan2.2-5B to yield a deployable 5B model (MobileWan).
AI.result: On-device generation of 5-second 480×832 videos at 16 FPS with 20 s end-to-end latency; VBench score of 83.79; first 5B-scale video diffusion model deployable on a commercial mobile device; achieves state-of-the-art for mobile video generation.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates that server-scale diffusion models can be adapted for mobile deployment through recurrence, attention sparsification, and efficient decoding, establishing a new benchmark and enabling high-quality on-device video generation.

title: Revisiting Scene Graph Generation from the Perspective of Detector-Conditioned Reachability
summary: Scene graph generation (SGG) approaches can be broadly classified into detector-based and query-based methods according to their underlying reasoning mechanisms. However, the discrepancy in their predictive behaviors, induced by these distinct mechanisms, has not been systematically analyzed. In this work, we design a controlled experimental setup to examine prediction discrepancies from the perspective of detector-conditioned reachability. The results suggest clear complementary clues. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a Dual-SGG method that consolidates both reasoning mechanisms via a dual-query design, thereby leveraging the complementary predictive behaviors of both detector-based and query-based methods. Extensive experiments on the Visual Genome, Open Images v6, and GQA-200 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: A study analyzes predictive discrepancies between detector-based and query-based SGG, introduces Dual-SGG with a dual-query design to fuse both, validated across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: There is a systematic discrepancy in predictions caused by the distinct reasoning mechanisms of detector-based and query-based SGG methods. The work seeks to understand these discrepancies and leverage their complementary signals by unifying them.
AI.method: Design a controlled experimental setup to examine prediction discrepancies via detector-conditioned reachability. Propose Dual-SGG, which uses a dual-query design to consolidate both reasoning mechanisms into a single framework.
AI.result: Experiments on Visual Genome, Open Images v6, and GQA-200 demonstrate the effectiveness of Dual-SGG, supporting the presence of complementary predictive behaviors and the benefit of integrating both mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: Dual-SGG successfully merges detector-based and query-based reasoning, yielding improved performance and robustness in scene graph generation across diverse datasets, and illustrating the value of combining heterogeneous reasoning modules.

title: Structured-Condensed Prompt Tuning in Vision-Language Models for Fine-grained Image Recognition
summary: Fine-grained image recognition poses a significant challenge due to the substantial expertise and effort required for manual annotation. Vision-language models (VLMs) like CLIP provide a compelling zero-shot alternative, reducing reliance on extensive labeled data. However, their ability to capture subtle distinctions remains limited, leading to subpar recognition performance. While prompt tuning has proven effective for adapting VLMs, most existing methods treat class labels as isolated, discrete entities, overlooking the rich semantic relationships between them. This oversimplified assumption limits the model's ability to capture hierarchical dependencies and inter-class correlations -- both critical for distinguishing visually similar categories. The problem is especially acute in fine-grained classification, where accurate recognition depends on understanding complex label semantics. To address this, we propose Structured-Condensed Prompt Tuning (SCPT), which enhances semantic structure modeling in prompt learning. Specifically, we introduce Semantic Relation Encoding (SRE) to explicitly model inter-class semantic topology and encode structured label relationships. In parallel, we design a Semantic Condensation loss (ScLoss) to suppress redundant supervision and extract discriminative components from the global semantic space. Together, these components significantly improve semantic alignment and fine-grained discrimination. Extensive experiments on 14 fine-grained benchmarks show that SCPT effectively mitigates semantic ambiguity and achieves state-of-the-art performance in both few-shot and base-to-novel generalization settings.

AI.tldr: SCPT introduces Semantic Relation Encoding and Semantic Condensation loss to refine prompt tuning for vision-language models in fine-grained recognition, modeling inter-class semantic relations and reducing redundant supervision, achieving state-of-the-art on 14 benchmarks in few-shot and base-to-novel settings.
AI.motivation: Current vision-language model prompt-tuning often treats class labels as isolated tokens, neglecting rich semantic relationships and hierarchical dependencies among fine-grained categories. This limits the models' ability to distinguish visually similar classes and exacerbates annotation burden.
AI.method: Propose Structured-Condensed Prompt Tuning (SCPT). It includes Semantic Relation Encoding (SRE) to explicitly model inter-class semantic topology and structured label relationships, and a Semantic Condensation loss (ScLoss) to suppress redundant supervision and extract discriminative components from the global semantic space. Integrated into the prompt learning framework to enhance semantic alignment and fine-grained discrimination.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on 14 fine-grained benchmarks demonstrate improved semantic alignment and discriminative power, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both few-shot and base-to-novel generalization settings.
AI.conclusion: Modeling structured label semantics within prompt tuning effectively mitigates semantic ambiguity and yields substantial gains in fine-grained recognition, highlighting the importance of semantic topology and condensed supervision in prompt-based VLM adaptation.

title: MoWorld: A Flash World Model
summary: The future of World Models depends not only on scaling model capability, but also on scaling practicality and inference efficiency. High-frame-rate inference enables responsive perception, planning, and control in real-world autonomous systems. To this end, we present MoWorld, a cost-effective yet high-performance Flash World Model with an end-to-end framework spanning data generation, pre-training, distillation, and efficient inference, enabling up to 50 FPS real-time interaction with cinematic visual quality without the need of high-end GPUs. To enable large-scale real-world deployment, MoWorld jointly optimizes model capability and cost throughout the entire development pipeline. Specifically, unlike existing approaches that primarily rely on large-scale video corpora, MoWorld is built upon a scalable 3D-native data engine accumulated from our large-scale 3D vision and generative modeling pipeline, enabling the efficient construction of geometrically consistent training data across diverse real-world and synthetic environments. Based on this foundation, a curriculum cross-frame pre-training strategy for stable and scalable World Model learning, an efficient denoising-step distillation algorithm to reduce diffusion training cost, and a mixed-precision parallel inference framework for low-cost real-time deployment. MoWorld is the first real-time interactive World Model built on the Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and can achieves up to 50 FPS in such the devices, enabling practical and efficient deployment at scale. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that MoWorld achieves leading performance; notably, its average inference cost is only 30\%-50\% of that of existing World Models, providing a practical foundation for large-scale real-world applications of World Models. We also demonstrate diverse applications of MoWorld.

AI.tldr: MoWorld is a cost-efficient, high-frame-rate world model enabling up to 50 FPS on NPUs through a 3D-native data engine, curriculum pre-training, diffusion-cost reduction via denoising distillation, and mixed-precision inference, achieving 30–50% inference cost compared to prior World Models.
AI.motivation: World Models require both scale in capability and practicality. High-frame-rate, real-time inference with low cost is essential for responsive perception, planning, and control in real-world autonomous systems, but existing approaches rely on expensive data, training costs, and high-end hardware.
AI.method: An end-to-end framework: (1) build a scalable 3D-native data engine for geometrically consistent real-world/synthetic data; (2) curriculum cross-frame pre-training for stable World Model learning; (3) efficient denoising-step distillation to cut diffusion training cost; (4) mixed-precision parallel inference for low-cost real-time deployment; (5) deploy on Neural Processing Unit (NPU) for up to 50 FPS; (6) end-to-end pipeline from data to inference.
AI.result: Demonstrates up to 50 FPS real-time interaction on NPUs with cinematic visual quality; average inference cost is 30–50% of existing World Models; comprehensive evaluations claim leading performance across evaluated metrics; multiple real-world applications demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: MoWorld offers a practical, scalable path for real-world deployment of World Models by jointly optimizing capability and cost across data, training, and inference, enabling real-time, cost-effective autonomous system applications.

title: EeveeDark: A Binary Neural Framework for Low-Light Video Enhancement via Event-Guided Sensor-Level Fusion
summary: Enhancing videos under extreme low-light conditions remains challenging due to the difficulty of balancing restoration quality and computational efficiency in resource-constrained settings. This paper introduces EeveeDark, a low-light video enhancement framework that combines the spatial richness of sensor-level RAW data with the temporal precision of event streams. Central to our model is a Binary Neural Network (BNN) architecture that reduces computational overhead by quantizing weights and activations while preserving detail. EeveeDark incorporates (i) modality-specific binary encoders for processing RAW frames and event data, (ii) a lightweight fusion block for integrating spatial and temporal cues, and (iii) an event-guided skip gating mechanism for dynamic spatiotemporal refinement. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that EeveeDark outperforms prior BNN-based methods and offers a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off compared to full-precision models. The project page is available at https://cyberiada.github.io/EeveeDark.

AI.tldr: EeveeDark is a low-light video enhancement framework that fuses RAW sensor frames with event data using a binary neural network to achieve high-quality restoration with reduced computation.
AI.motivation: To address extreme low-light video restoration under resource constraints by leveraging both high-spatial-quality RAW data and temporally precise event streams, while maintaining efficiency with quantized (binary) networks.
AI.method: EeveeDark adopts modality-specific binary encoders for RAW frames and event data, a lightweight fusion block to combine spatial and temporal cues, and an event-guided skip gating mechanism for dynamic spatiotemporal refinement, all built atop Binary Neural Network (BNN) principles to quantize weights and activations.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show EeveeDark outperforms prior BNN-based methods and achieves a favorable performance-efficiency balance compared to full-precision models.
AI.conclusion: EeveeDark demonstrates that combining RAW+event data with BNNs can deliver competitive video enhancement quality under strict compute budgets; a project page is provided for further details.

title: WING: A Window-Prior-Based Generative Network with Gated Inception for Cross-Modality CT Synthesis
summary: Generating CT volumes from MRI and CBCT can improve treatment planning in adaptive radiotherapy while avoiding additional radiation exposure. However, direct regression of CT intensities is challenged by the inherently high dynamic range and long-tailed distributions, thereby averaging out sparse yet clinically important structures. To alleviate this issue, we reformulate the regression target into multiple windowed representations, leveraging the inductive prior that CT intensities are structure-deterministic and window-separable. These windowed views exhibit smoother distributions and admit structured fusion back to the full-range CT. Building on this reformulation, we introduce WING, a WINdow-prior-based Generative network comprising: 1) a new Gated Inception Generator to produce multi-window predictions, enabling multi-shape kernel interactions to capture cross-modality correspondence; 2) a Fuse-and-Refine Transformer to aggregate the windowed outputs and learn residuals for detail refinement; and 3) a joint adversarial training objective to enhance window-conditioned realism. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our compact WING achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MRI-to-CT and CBCT-to-CT benchmarks, while supporting multi-anatomy synthesis with a single model.

AI.tldr: A window-prior-based generative framework (WING) for MRI/CBCT-to-CT synthesis using multi-window regression, Gated Inception Generator, Fuse-and-Refine Transformer, and adversarial training; achieves state-of-the-art on MRI-to-CT and CBCT-to-CT with a single model for multi-anatomy.
AI.motivation: CT intensities span a high dynamic range with long-tailed distributions, causing regression to average out sparse but clinically important structures. A structure-deterministic, window-separable prior via multiple window representations stabilizes learning and preserves details.
AI.method: 1) Reformulate CT regression as multiple windowed views; 2) Gated Inception Generator to produce multi-window predictions with cross-kernel interactions; 3) Fuse-and-Refine Transformer to fuse windowed outputs and learn residuals for fine detail; 4) Joint adversarial objective to enforce window-conditioned realism.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on MRI-to-CT and CBCT-to-CT benchmarks; compact model; supports multi-anatomy synthesis with a single model.
AI.conclusion: Window-prior-based WING improves CT synthesis by leveraging structured windowed representations and fusion, enabling robust cross-modality and multi-anatomy generation and potential benefits for adaptive radiotherapy planning.

title: PhyMRI-SR: Toward Physics-Aware MRI Image Super-Resolution
summary: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) super-resolution is vital for improving diagnostic accessibility, yet most methods treat it as a deterministic mapping from a fixed low-resolution input to a high-resolution target. This overlooks a key property of MRI acquisition physics: spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) are inherently coupled, making any given low-resolution scan merely one of many possible realizations under varying acquisition trade-offs. We rethink MRI super-resolution as a physics-aware reconstruction problem, in which the goal is to identify the optimal resolution-SNR configuration and then super-resolve it to obtain high-quality MRI results. A key implication of this formulation is that MRI resolution becomes dynamic rather than fixed. To handle such resolution-heterogeneous inputs, we adapt 2D Gaussian Splatting (2D GS) to MRI by formulating reconstruction as a coordinate-based, resolution-agnostic rendering problem. To further enhance fidelity, we introduce three innovations: (1) a prior-aware Gaussian representation that combines an Anatomical Structure Prior for tissue-specific kernel initialization with an Imaging System Prior that captures hardware characteristics via a covariance dictionary; (2) a physics-constrained signal modeling scheme that predicts intrinsic tissue parameters (proton density rho and effective relaxation rate R2) and synthesizes intensities through governing physical equations, ensuring biophysically plausible contrast; and (3) a meta-learning framework that alleviates paired-data scarcity by pretraining on simulated data and adapting to real-world conditions. Extensive experiments on dynamic-resolution datasets and standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, highlighting its strong potential for clinical deployment.

AI.tldr: Reframes MRI super-resolution as a physics-aware, resolution-agnostic reconstruction using dynamic resolution–SNR trade-offs, via a 2D Gaussian Splatting-based pipeline with priors, physics-based modeling, and meta-learning for robust, data-efficient SR.
AI.motivation: MRI acquisitions couple spatial resolution and SNR; treating SR as a deterministic, fixed-input mapping ignores acquisition physics and limits clinical transfer. A physics-aware, dynamic-resolution framework aims to identify optimal resolution-SNR configuration and robustly reconstruct high-quality images.
AI.method: Adapt 2D Gaussian Splatting to MRI as a coordinate-based, resolution-agnostic renderer. Propose a prior-aware Gaussian representation with Anatomical Structure Prior (tissue-specific kernel initialization) and Imaging System Prior (covariance dictionary reflecting hardware characteristics). Introduce physics-constrained signal modeling predicting intrinsic tissue parameters (rho, R2) and synthesizing intensities via governing equations. Employ a meta-learning framework pretrained on simulated data and adapted to real-world data to mitigate paired-data scarcity.
AI.result: On dynamic-resolution datasets and standard benchmarks, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance, indicating strong fidelity across varying acquisition settings and promising clinical deployment potential.
AI.conclusion: A physics-aware, dynamic-resolution MR-SR framework that integrates priors, physics-based signal modeling, and meta-learning to handle acquisition heterogeneity and data scarcity, yielding superior performance and clinical relevance.

title: VendorBench-100: A Unified Cross-Paradigm Benchmark for Deepfake Image Detection
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/sharayu-20/vendorbench-100
summary: Deepfake image detection is currently served by three fundamentally different paradigms: commercial APIs, zero-shot vision-language models (LLMs), and open-source detectors. Despite their widespread use, these paradigms are rarely evaluated under a common protocol, making direct comparison difficult. We introduce VendorBench-100, a cross-paradigm benchmark that evaluates 36 representative models using a single adversarial 100-image corpus, a unified output schema, and a common evaluation framework. To ensure reliable assessment under the corpus's intentional class imbalance, models are ranked primarily by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), with ROC-AUC reported as a threshold-independent measure of ranking ability. Rather than maximizing dataset size, VendorBench-100 emphasizes challenging real-world scenarios through a curated taxonomy of eight edge-case families, including face swaps, text-to-video stills, AI photo edits, avatar compositing, opaque-provenance images, and compressed research frames. Our evaluation shows that commercial APIs achieve the strongest median performance, followed by vision LLMs and open-source detectors. However, individual open-source models remain competitive with the best vision LLMs. More importantly, we identify a consistent divergence between ranking ability (ROC-AUC) and operating-point quality (MCC), demonstrating that strong score discrimination does not necessarily produce reliable default-threshold decisions. This metric disagreement, rather than any single leaderboard ranking, is the central finding of the benchmark. We release the complete evaluation framework and benchmark results to support reproducible future research. The source code and data are available at: https://github.com/sharayu-20/vendorbench-100

AI.tldr: VendorBench-100 offers a cross-paradigm, 100-image deepfake benchmark across 36 models (commercial APIs, zero-shot vision-language models, and open-source detectors) using a unified protocol. It ranks by MCC due to class imbalance and reports ROC-AUC for threshold-independent ranking, evaluating eight edge-case families. Results show commercial APIs lead in median performance, with LLMs and open-source detectors following; notable divergence between ranking (ROC-AUC) and operating-point quality (MCC), highlighting threshold reliability as a core issue.
AI.motivation: There is no unified, cross-paradigm benchmark for deepfake detection; existing evaluations under disparate protocols hinder fair comparison and real-world reliability, especially under imbalanced data and edge-case scenarios.
AI.method: Construct VendorBench-100 with a 100-image adversarial corpus framed around eight edge-case families (e.g., face swaps, AI edits, avatar compositing, compressed frames). Normalize outputs to a single schema and evaluate 36 models from three paradigms under a common framework. Use MCC as the primary ranking metric to handle class imbalance, and report ROC-AUC as a threshold-independent ranking measure; analyze discrepancies between metrics and across paradigms.
AI.result: Commercial APIs exhibit the strongest median performance, followed by vision LLMs and open-source detectors; several open-source models are competitive with top LLMs. A consistent divergence is observed between ROC-AUC-based ranking and MCC-based operating-point quality, underscoring that strong discriminative scores do not guarantee reliable threshold decisions. The authors provide the evaluation framework and results for reproducibility.
AI.conclusion: Metric disagreement between ranking ability (ROC-AUC) and operating-point reliability (MCC) is the central finding. VendorBench-100 offers a reproducible, cross-paradigm evaluation framework and dataset to guide future deepfake detection research and fair comparisons across detectors.

title: MAC-XA: Multi-view Anatomy-Correspondence Fusion for Coronary Stenosis Reporting from X-ray Angiography
summary: Multi-view reasoning in coronary X-ray angiography is inherently a cross-projection geometric problem, yet automated report generation in this setting remains largely unexplored. The 3D vascular topology leads to projection-dependent branch overlap and foreshortening, rendering single-view modeling fundamentally incomplete and unstable for lesion localization and stenosis grading. Although multi-view fusion appears promising, learning anatomically consistent fusion from real angiograms is impeded by a critical limitation: cross-view alignment is unobservable and cannot be explicitly supervised. Consequently, conventional fusion relies on implicit correlations rather than verified anatomical correspondence. We address this by reformulating multi-view stenosis reporting as an alignment-constrained aggregation problem. A controllable synthetic angiography generation strategy is introduced to expose geometry-derived patch-level correspondence supervision unavailable in real data. An anatomy-correspondence module learns cross-view correspondence matrices that explicitly align auxiliary features within the main-view coordinate space prior to fusion, thereby constraining evidence aggregation to anatomically consistent regions. Experiments on synthetic data and zero-shot transfer to real angiograms show that this alignment-constrained design improves correspondence consistency and structured stenosis reporting compared to single-view modeling and conventional multi-view fusion methods. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

AI.tldr: Proposes an alignment-constrained multi-view fusion framework for coronary angiography that learns anatomy-consistent cross-view correspondences via synthetic data supervision to improve stenosis reporting.
AI.motivation: Cross-projection geometry causes projection-dependent overlap and foreshortening in coronary angiography; single-view models are incomplete; cross-view alignment is unobservable and cannot be supervised, making traditional fusion rely on implicit correlations.
AI.method: Introduce an anatomy-correspondence module that learns cross-view correspondence matrices to align auxiliary features into the main-view space before fusion; use a controllable synthetic angiography generation strategy to provide geometry-derived, patch-level supervision unavailable in real data; optimize alignment-constrained evidence aggregation.
AI.result: On synthetic data and zero-shot transfer to real angiograms, the method improves correspondence consistency and structured stenosis reporting over single-view models and conventional multi-view fusion methods.
AI.conclusion: Alignment-constrained cross-view fusion enables anatomically consistent multi-view stenosis reporting in angiography and leverages synthetic supervision to overcome unobservable cross-view alignment; code will be released.

title: Straight-Path Flow Matching for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. 28 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables
summary: Incomplete Multi-View Clustering addresses the problem of clustering multi-modal data when certain views are missing. Recent end-to-end generative approaches leverage diffusion models to recover missing views via stochastic noise-to-data trajectories. While expressive, such mechanisms are not explicitly designed for clustering, as they initialize from cluster-agnostic noise and rely on stochastic denoising dynamics. In this work, we revisit probability path design in end-to-end generative IMVC. We introduce a flow-matching framework with a linear interpolation path between paired view representations, that replaces diffusion with probability flows between observed and missing views. We provide a formal analysis showing that deterministic ODE flows are inherently better aligned with clustering objectives than diffusion-based stochastic trajectories, especially in terms of transport mechanisms that respect class-conditional data distributions and maintain cluster consistency in finite-step regimes. Building upon this insight, we develop an end-to-end IMVC architecture that integrates straight-path flow-matching view completion with cluster-level and entropy-based alignment to enforce cross-view clustering consistency. Extensive experiments on standard IMVC benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework establishes new state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: Deterministic flow-matching for incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) using a straight-path interpolation between views replaces diffusion with probability flows, yielding state-of-the-art clustering performance.
AI.motivation: Tackle limitations of diffusion-based IMVC models (cluster-agnostic noise initialization and stochastic denoising) by designing a transport that preserves class-conditional structure and improves clustering consistency.
AI.method: Propose a flow-matching framework with a linear interpolation path between paired view representations, substituting stochastic diffusion with deterministic ODE flows; integrate cluster-level and entropy-based alignment into an end-to-end IMVC architecture.
AI.result: Experiments on standard IMVC benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.
AI.conclusion: Deterministic ODE flow transports align better with clustering objectives than diffusion in IMVC, yielding improved cross-view clustering consistency and performance.

title: AlayaWorld: Long-Horizon and Playable Video World Generation
comment: Authors are listed alphabetically by the first name and their role. See the contribution section for details
summary: Game worlds have traditionally been built through labor-intensive production pipelines, making them costly to develop, difficult to customization, and expensive to modify after deployment. Recent advances in video world models offer a fundamentally different paradigm. Rather than explicitly authoring every component of a virtual environment, these models autoregressively synthesize future observations conditioned on the current world state and user interactions, enabling playable worlds to be generated online. Trained on both gameplay recordings and real-world videos, they can capture diverse visual appearances and physical dynamics, opening new opportunities for interactive applications beyond gaming, including embodied intelligence. In this paper, we present \textbf{AlayaWorld}, a full-stack open-source framework for building interactive generative worlds. AlayaWorld enables open-ended real-time interaction, allowing users to freely navigate and perform diverse actions such as combat, spell casting, and monster summoning. The framework unifies the complete development-from data preparation model architecture, model training, inference acceleration, and deployment-within a modular and extensible architecture. Alongside the framework, we release reproducible pipelines, reference implementations, evaluation tools, and comprehensive documentation, establishing a practical foundation for future research and real-time applications of generative world models.

AI.tldr: AlayaWorld is a full-stack, open-source framework for building interactive generative game-like worlds that can synthesize future observations in real time from current state and user actions, enabling open-ended play.
AI.motivation: Traditional game development relies on labor-intensive pipelines and fixed assets, making customization and post-deployment modification costly. Advances in video world models enable online, autoregressive generation of playable environments by learning from gameplay and real-world videos, unlocking interactive applications beyond gaming.
AI.method: A modular, open-source stack that unifies data preparation, model architecture, training, inference acceleration, and deployment. The model is trained on gameplay recordings and real-world videos to capture diverse visuals and dynamics. It supports real-time interaction (e.g., combat, spell casting, monster summoning) and provides reproducible pipelines, reference implementations, evaluation tools, and documentation.
AI.result: The paper presents AlayaWorld as a practical foundation for building interactive generative worlds, delivering a ready-to-use framework and tools to enable real-time, open-ended interaction and accelerate research and development in generative world models.
AI.conclusion: AlayaWorld establishes a concrete, usable platform that lowers the barrier to research and deployment of interactive generative worlds, facilitating future work and real-time applications in this domain.

title: Visual graphs for image classification: does the structure affect performance?
summary: Deep learning models have emerged in machine learning and related fields, demonstrating astonishing performance in various visual tasks. Despite their great success, however, these models are unable to fully encode intrinsic visual structures, and often ignore the spatial, topological, and semantic information contained within an image. Graph neural networks offer a good framework to face this aspect, but their effective use for visual tasks has been only partly explored and mainly starting from a limited perspective. This work aims to address this gap by conducting a systematic comparison of current graph construction techniques within the context of a fixed three-layer GCN architecture. Through an empirical study, it demonstrates in particular how the network structure affects performance and provides an important methodological contribution regarding the computational stages preceding graph utilization, which will be strongly influenced by the structure itself.

AI.tldr: Systematic empirical comparison of graph construction techniques for visual tasks using a fixed 3-layer GCN, showing that graph design and preprocessing stages markedly influence performance.
AI.motivation: Graph neural networks hold promise for encoding intrinsic visual structures, but the literature lacks a thorough, systematic study of how graph construction choices affect performance in visual tasks; understanding preprocessing stages is essential since they are shaped by the graph structure.
AI.method: An empirical study employing a fixed three-layer GCN, comparing multiple graph construction techniques, and analyzing the computational stages preceding graph utilization to reveal how graph structure influences the training and inference pipeline.
AI.result: Network performance is significantly affected by the chosen graph construction technique. The study also highlights the strong influence of preprocessing steps and their interaction with the graph structure, indicating that some constructions yield substantially better results within the same GCN architecture.
AI.conclusion: The work provides methodological guidance for graph construction and preprocessing in visual GCNs, emphasizing that careful consideration of graph structure is crucial for achieving optimal performance and efficient computation.

title: Token-Based Dual-view Fusion and Adaptation of Large Vision Models for Breast Cancer Classification
summary: Accurate breast cancer classification from mammography requires effective integration of complementary information from craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views, which provide a more complete characterization of breast abnormalities. However, existing multi-view learning approaches typically rely on feature-level aggregation or single-stage cross-attention, which can entangle view-specific and shared representations and restrict interaction to limited network depths. To address these limitations, we propose a token-centric dual-view learning framework that unifies prompt-based adaptation and cross-view fusion within a frozen vision transformer backbone. The framework reformulates inter-view interaction as structured token-level communication, where dedicated fusion tokens explicitly encode bidirectional information exchange between CC and MLO views via cross-attention, serving as intermediate carriers of cross-view dependencies rather than relying on direct feature fusion. Unlike conventional methods that apply fusion at a single layer, fusion modules are inserted at multiple transformer depths, enabling progressive and repeated interaction across the encoder hierarchy. Fusion tokens are reintegrated into the token sequence and refined by subsequent transformer layers, facilitating hierarchical propagation of complementary information while preserving view-specific structure. Experiments on VinDr-Mammo and CMMD datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over linear probing, prompt-only adaptation, and conventional fusion baselines. On the VinDr-Mammo BI-RADS classification task, the framework achieves 50.40% F1-score and 0.8090 AUC, including a 0.10 AUC improvement over a dual-view fusion baseline in the binary setting. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of token-based fusion and multi-depth interaction design.

AI.tldr: A token-centric dual-view framework for multimodal breast cancer classification from CC and MLO mammography views uses cross-view fusion tokens inserted at multiple depths in a frozen ViT backbone, achieving improvements over baselines on VinDr-Mammo and CMMD.
AI.motivation: Leverage complementary information from two mammography views (CC and MLO) more effectively than existing feature-level fusion or single-stage cross-attention, by enabling iterative, token-level cross-view interaction within a frozen transformer backbone.
AI.method: Replace direct feature fusion with dedicated fusion tokens that carry cross-view information via cross-attention. Insert fusion modules at multiple transformer depths to enable progressive interaction. Reinforce view-specific tokens by reintegrating fusion tokens into the sequence for further transformer processing, enabling hierarchical propagation of complementary information. Also incorporates prompt-based adaptation within a frozen ViT backbone.
AI.result: On VinDr-Mammo BI-RADS classification: F1 50.40% and AUC 0.8090, with +0.10 AUC over a dual-view fusion baseline in binary setting. Also validated on CMMD dataset; ablation studies verify effectiveness of token-based fusion and multi-depth interaction; outperforms linear probing and prompt-only adaptation.
AI.conclusion: Token-based fusion with multi-depth interaction within a frozen ViT enables structured, hierarchical cross-view information exchange, improving multimodal performance for mammography BI-RADS classification over conventional fusion baselines and simpler adaptation strategies.

title: Synthetic-to-Real Translation for Class-Agnostic Motion Prediction
summary: Motion understanding is critical for ensuring safety and robustness in autonomous driving systems, driving increasing interest in motion prediction. A key challenge in this domain is the high cost associated with acquiring real-world motion labels. It is therefore ideal if we could transfer motion knowledge from synthetic data to real data. In this context, we explore the potential of synthetic-to-real translation for motion prediction (SRMP). However, the most used naive motion regression methods are notably sensitive to the synthetic-to-real domain shift, resulting in unreliable knowledge translation. To address this, we propose a novel approach integrating a motion knowledge translation framework with two key components: (1) objectness-aware motion prediction, which explicitly models the joint distribution of motion patterns and objectness priors to improve domain-invariant feature learning, and (2) objectness-aided motion enhancement, a motion label refinement mechanism that leverages learned objectness priors to filter motion noise. Furthermore, we present a physically-based pipeline for generating Motion4D, the first synthetic 4D LiDAR dataset tailored for SRMP research, addressing the lack of synthetic motion datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively bridges the domain gaps and yields superior performance on real scenes.

AI.tldr: Introduces SRMP: a synthetic-to-real translation framework for motion prediction with two components (objectness-aware motion prediction and objectness-aided motion enhancement) and a pipeline for a synthetic 4D LiDAR dataset (Motion4D); reports improved real-scene performance through domain adaptation.
AI.motivation: High cost and limited availability of real-world motion labels for autonomous driving; synthetic data offers scalable supervision but suffers from domain shift when transferring to real data. A synthetic-to-real translation approach for motion prediction (SRMP) is proposed to bridge this gap.
AI.method: 1) Objectness-aware motion prediction that models the joint distribution of motion patterns and objectness priors to learn domain-invariant features. 2) Objectness-aided motion enhancement that refines motion labels by leveraging learned objectness priors to filter noise. 3) A physically-based pipeline for generating Motion4D, a synthetic 4D LiDAR dataset tailored for SRMP, addressing lack of synthetic motion datasets.
AI.result: Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework reduces the synthetic-to-real domain gap and yields superior performance on real scenes, verifying effective knowledge transfer for motion prediction.
AI.conclusion: The work advances SRMP by combining objectness-informed probability modeling with label refinement and contributes the Motion4D synthetic 4D LiDAR dataset, enabling more robust motion prediction under domain shift.

title: What Images Cannot Say: Language-Guided Olfactory Representation Learning
summary: Images tell us what a scene looks like, but rarely what it would feel like to be there. While recent datasets pair visual scenes with electronic-nose measurements, aligning smell signals with images remains challenging because many olfactory cues arise from contextual environmental factors that are not directly visible in pixels. We introduce SCENT, a multimodal framework that uses language guidance as a semantic bridge between vision and olfaction. Our approach leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to generate scene descriptors capturing objects, environmental context, and plausible ambient smell cues suggested by the visual scene. These descriptors provide semantic guidance for learning olfactory representations. We train a smell encoder that maps electronic-nose signals into a shared embedding space aligned with both visual and textual representations, and introduce a languageguided latent decomposition that separates object-specific odors from contextual environmental contributions. Experiments on the New York Smells dataset demonstrate that SCENT significantly improves crossmodal retrieval compared to vision-only baselines, achieving state-of-theart performance on smell-to-image and smell-to-text retrieval tasks. In addition, our framework produces interpretable olfactory representations that enable the disentanglement of complex smell mixtures. Our results reveal the importance of contextual semantic information for grounding olfactory perception in multimodal learning and pave the way for future research in this area.

AI.tldr: SCENT grounds olfactory signals in a shared semantic space using language-guided vision-language models to align smell with vision and text, enabling improved crossmodal retrieval and interpretable odor representations.
AI.motivation: Olfactory signals are heavily context-dependent and not directly visible; bridging smell with visual data requires semantic grounding to disentangle percepts from contextual cues.
AI.method: Leverage Vision-Language Models to generate scene descriptors (objects, context, ambient smell cues). Train a smell encoder to map electronic-nose signals into a shared embedding space aligned with visual and textual representations. Introduce a language-guided latent decomposition to separate object-specific odors from contextual environmental contributions.
AI.result: On the New York Smells dataset, SCENT significantly improves crossmodal retrieval over vision-only baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance for smell-to-image and smell-to-text retrieval. The framework also yields interpretable olfactory representations that disentangle complex smell mixtures.
AI.conclusion: Contextual semantic information is crucial for grounding olfactory perception in multimodal learning, and SCENT lays groundwork for future research in vision–olfaction understanding.

title: Bridging Diffusion Pruning and Step Distillation with Teacher-Aligned Repair
summary: Diffusion models generate high-quality images, but their inference cost comes from two sources: large denoising networks and repeated denoising steps. Existing compression pipelines usually attack these costs separately. Pruning reduces the network, but most pruning methods still rely on a long post-pruning retraining stage to recover a many-step sampler. Step distillation reduces the number of denoising steps, but it usually assumes a student that can already follow the teacher well enough to receive useful distillation gradients. This paper asks whether post-pruning retraining can be replaced by step distillation. We find that the direct replacement fails: after pruning an EDM2-XS teacher, starting SiDA from the pruned checkpoint produces unusable samples. We introduce a short teacher-alignment repair stage as a bridge between pruning and step distillation. The bridge matches the pruned generator to the teacher on noisy real-image latents, then hands the repaired checkpoint to one-step distillation. On ImageNet-512, the original EDM2-XS baseline uses 124.713M parameters and 63 network evaluations, reaching an FID of 3.53. With a suitable distillation objective, our 20% pruned one-step generator uses 98.826M parameters and one network evaluation, reaching an FID of 3.12. With 30% pruning, the model uses 88.029M parameters and one network evaluation, with an FID of 4.26.

AI.tldr: Bridging pruning and step distillation for diffusion models via a brief teacher-alignment repair stage, enabling one-step distillation after pruning, with promising results on ImageNet-512.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models incur high inference cost from large denoising networks and many denoising steps. Existing compression methods tackle these costs separately (pruning vs step distillation) and often require lengthy post-pruning retraining. The paper investigates whether post-pruning retraining can be replaced by step distillation, and identifies a repair step as necessary to align the pruned generator with the teacher before distillation.
AI.method: 1) Prune the EDM2-XS teacher (e.g., 20% or 30% pruning). 2) Introduce a short teacher-alignment repair stage that matches the pruned generator to the teacher on noisy real-image latents. 3) Perform one-step distillation (SiDA) using the repaired checkpoint. 4) Evaluate on ImageNet-512, comparing to the baseline and varying pruning levels.
AI.result: Baseline EDM2-XS: 124.713M parameters, 63 network evaluations, FID 3.53. After 20% pruning with one-step distillation: 98.826M params, 1 evaluation, FID 3.12. After 30% pruning with one-step distillation: 88.029M params, 1 evaluation, FID 4.26.
AI.conclusion: A short teacher-alignment repair bridge enables effective one-step distillation after pruning, mitigating the need for lengthy post-pruning retraining. The approach yields substantial parameter reduction and fast inference with competitive or improved fidelity (notably 20% pruning achieves the best FID among the reported configurations).

title: Generalized Synthetic Image Detection with Enhanced RGB-Noise Representation Learning
summary: The rapid advancement of large-scale generative models has accelerated the spread of highly deceptive AI-generated images, making generalized synthetic image detection a critical imperative. Existing forensic networks often struggle with cross-model generalization and realworld degradations due to their reliance on single-domain representations and conventional binary classification optimization. To overcome these limitations, we propose RNSIDNet, a novel forensic framework that achieves robust detection through enhanced RGB-Noise representation learning. Specifically, our method employs a dual-branch architecture where global RGB semantics, extracted by an attention-refined CLIP backbone, dynamically modulate highfrequency noise artifacts captured by Bayar convolutions via a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) module. To further enhance the learned representations, we design a Hard Sample-aware Contrastive Learning (HSCL) strategy. By explicitly penalizing challenging training samples, HSCL reshapes the latent feature space to maximize the discriminative margin between pristine and synthetic domains. Extensive experiments across eight public benchmark datasets verify that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance, delivering superior generalization ability, robustness, and computational efficiency. Code and dataset will be publicly available on https://github.com/multimediaFor/RNSIDNet.

AI.tldr: RNSIDNet introduces a dual-branch RGB-Noise forensic framework with CLIP-based RGB semantics and Bayar high-frequency features, modulated by FiLM, plus Hard Sample-aware Contrastive Learning, achieving state-of-the-art cross-model generalization in AI-generated image detection.
AI.motivation: Address poor cross-model generalization and vulnerability to real-world degradations in single-domain, binary-classifiers forensic nets used for synthetic image detection.
AI.method: A dual-branch architecture: (1) attention-refined CLIP backbone extracts global RGB semantics; (2) Bayar convolutions capture high-frequency noise; FiLM module fuses via modulation; Hard Sample-aware Contrastive Learning to penalize difficult samples and shape latent space.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on eight public benchmarks show state-of-the-art results with improved generalization, robustness, and efficiency; code will be released.
AI.conclusion: RNSIDNet provides a robust, generalizable framework for synthetic image detection through enhanced RGB-Noise representations and hard-sample contrastive learning, addressing cross-model and degradations challenges.

title: ELSA3D: Elastic Semantic Anchoring for Unified 3D Understanding and Generation
summary: Unified 3D foundation models aspire to generate 3D assets and reason about them in language within a single backbone, but their text-3D interaction remains largely implicit. Existing methods concatenate text and 3D tokens into a flat sequence and rely on self-attention, collapsing coarse structural cues and fine geometric details into one undifferentiated representation. We introduce ELSA3D, a unified 3D model that addresses this with elastic semantic anchoring, structuring language and geometric reasoning jointly along matched abstraction scales. ELSA3D represents geometry with a scale-aware octree tokenizer and introduces Anchor Tokens, sparse cross-modal units that select semantic cues, route them to the most relevant 3D scale, retrieve scale-specific geometric evidence, and write the fused signal back into the unified representation, keeping interaction sparse yet precise. A lightweight per-block router makes both computation and reasoning elastic, choosing which text tokens instantiate anchors at which geometric scale so that cross-modal capacity concentrates where alignment is most needed. ELSA3D achieves state-of-the-art performance across image-to-3D generation, text-to-3D generation, and 3D captioning, outperforming the strongest unified baseline while roughly halving FLOPs and inference latency relative to the non-elastic version of the same model.

AI.tldr: ELSA3D introduces elastic semantic anchoring to unify text-3D reasoning by matching language and geometry across scales with a scale-aware octree tokenizer and Anchor Tokens, enabling sparse, scale-aligned cross-modal fusion that improves performance while cutting compute.
AI.motivation: Current unified 3D foundation models fuse text and 3D tokens in a single flat sequence, which loses coarse structural cues and fine geometric details. There is a need for a mechanism that preserves multi-scale structure and enables selective, efficient cross-modal alignment.
AI.method: Propose a scale-aware octree tokenizer to represent geometry. Introduce Anchor Tokens, sparse cross-modal units that select semantic cues, route them to the relevant 3D scale, retrieve scale-specific geometric evidence, and write fused signals back into a unified representation. A lightweight per-block router decides which text tokens instantiate anchors at which geometric scale, keeping interaction sparse.
AI.result: ELSA3D achieves state-of-the-art results on image-to-3D generation, text-to-3D generation, and 3D captioning, outperforming the strongest unified baseline and reducing FLOPs and inference latency by roughly 50% compared to the non-elastic version of the same model.
AI.conclusion: Elastic semantic anchoring with scale-aware geometry yields precise, efficient cross-modal fusion in a unified 3D model, enabling better performance with substantially reduced compute and latency.

title: TMF-RSE: Tri-Modal Fusion with Regional Semantics and Evidential Uncertainty for Lung Severity Scoring
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. IEEE conference format (IEEEtran). Submitted to AVSS 2026. Tri-modal fusion for lung severity scoring using appearance, segmentation, and VLM semantics with evidential uncertainty
summary: Accurate quantification of lung disease severity from chest imaging is critical for clinical decision-making and resource allocation. We propose a tri-modal deep learning framework, TMF-RSE (Tri-Modal Fusion with Regional Semantics and Evidential Uncertainty), that combines appearance features from two-dimensional chest inputs, structural features from lung segmentation masks, and semantic features from vision-language models (VLMs) for severity quantification. Our approach employs complementary fusion mechanisms that integrate semantic guidance, structural priors, and hierarchical interactions across modalities. The model employs evidential regression to provide both severity predictions and uncertainty estimates. Experiments on the Per-COVID-19 CT and RALO datasets show that TMF-RSE outperforms recent transformer-based baselines, achieving MAE of 4.02 and Pearson correlation of 0.9629 on Per-COVID-19 validation, and 0.339 MAE / 0.973 PC on RALO geographic extent.

AI.tldr: A tri-modal fusion framework (TMF-RSE) combines appearance, structural, and semantic features with evidential regression to quantify lung disease severity from chest imaging, achieving strong results on Per-COVID-19 CT and RALO datasets and providing uncertainty estimates.
AI.motivation: Accurate and reliable quantification of lung disease severity from imaging is critical for clinical decisions and resource allocation. Leveraging complementary information from image appearance, anatomical structures, and high-level semantic cues can improve robustness and generalization, while uncertainty estimates support risk-aware decision making.
AI.method: TMF-RSE uses tri-modal fusion: (1) appearance features from 2D chest inputs, (2) structural priors from lung segmentation masks, and (3) semantic features from vision-language models. Fusion includes semantic guidance, structural priors, and hierarchical cross-modal interactions. The model employs evidential regression to output severity predictions along with uncertainty estimates.
AI.result: On Per-COVID-19 CT: MAE 4.02 and Pearson correlation 0.9629 on validation. On RALO dataset: MAE 0.339 and Pearson correlation 0.973 for geographic extent. TMF-RSE outperforms recent transformer-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: TMF-RSE demonstrates effective multi-modal fusion for robust severity quantification with quantified uncertainty, indicating potential clinical value for decision support and resource planning. Further validation across diverse datasets and ablation analyses would help assess generalizability and the contribution of each modality.

title: VaseMuseum: Digital Intelligent Museum for Ancient Greek Pottery
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have made interactive digital museums increasingly feasible by connecting 3D digitization with natural-language artifact exploration. However, in cultural heritage domains such as ancient Greek pottery, reliable VLM assistance is limited by two challenges. First, open-ended interpretation requires grounding fine-grained 2D/3D visual evidence in specialized curatorial knowledge, yet the retrieval process may introduce weak sources and unverifiable references. Second, when the available evidence is incomplete, noisy, or ambiguous, VLMs often produce confident but unsupported answers instead of calibrated uncertainty. To address these challenges, we propose VaseMuseum, a lightweight and modular multimodal agent framework for intelligent digital museums of ancient Greek pottery. VaseMuseum combines an interactive virtual museum with VaseAgent, which supports both 2D images and 3D artifacts through multimodal perception, 3D-aware reasoning, external knowledge retrieval, and inference-time reliability control. Specifically, VaseAgent retrieves evidence from authoritative web and museum knowledge sources, and source-level control selects diverse and verifiable evidence before generation. Meanwhile, response-level control checks generated claims against the evidence pool and encourages neutral, evidence-bounded answers when support is insufficient or conflicting. Moreover, a training-free GRPO-style selection mechanism favors responses with valid references and calibrated confidence without updating the VLM backbone. Experiments in a realistic digital museum simulation show that VaseMuseum improves citation validity, reduces hallucinations on knowledge-intensive queries, and produces more neutral answers under ambiguity compared with search-enabled VLM baselines.

AI.tldr: A modular, training-free, multimodal agent (VaseMuseum/VaseAgent) improves VLM reliability for ancient Greek pottery by grounded evidence retrieval and calibrated, evidence-bounded responses, outperforming search-enabled baselines.
AI.motivation: Grounding fine-grained visual evidence to specialized curatorial knowledge is error-prone; retrieved sources can be weak or unverifiable; when evidence is incomplete, noisy, or ambiguous, VLMs often produce overconfident but unsupported answers.
AI.method: Propose VaseMuseum with VaseAgent: multimodal perception for 2D images and 3D artifacts; 3D-aware reasoning; external knowledge retrieval; source-level control for diverse and verifiable evidence; response-level control to constrain claims to evidence; training-free GRPO-style selection to favor valid references and calibrated confidence; no backbone update.
AI.result: In a digital museum simulation, VaseMuseum yields higher citation validity, fewer hallucinations on knowledge-intensive queries, and more neutral answers under ambiguity versus search-enabled VLM baselines.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates a lightweight, modular approach to improving reliability and calibration in VLM-based digital museums for cultural heritage, reducing misinformation and supporting calibrated exploration.

title: FADRA: Frequency-Aware Diffusion with Residual Adaptation for Video Face Restoration
summary: Video face restoration (VFR) aims to recover high-quality and temporally consistent facial details from severely degraded video sequences; however, existing methods still struggle to balance spatial fidelity and temporal coherence under complex degradations. To address this, we propose FADRA, a frequency-aware diffusion framework with iterative residual adaptation specifically tailored for robust VFR. We first leverage the strong temporal consistency of a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion model and introduce lightweight LoRA adapters together with a Low-Quality (LQ) Pixel-Alignment Feature Fusion module to efficiently adapt the frozen generative prior to the VFR task. To further adapt the frozen diffusion backbone to the downstream VFR task beyond LoRA-based adaptation, we introduce a Repeated Residual Adaptation Head (RRAH) for step-wise residual refinement after the diffusion backbone. To make this refinement explicitly guided by the degraded observation, RRAH further takes the LQ latent together with the current velocity prediction as input, allowing the model to repeatedly revisit LQ cues and predict residual updates at each flow-matching step. This LQ-guided repeated residual adaptation helps recover fine facial details while preserving the inherent temporal priors of the pre-trained model. Furthermore, to ensure the structural integrity of perceptually important details, we introduce a Frequency-Aware Loss that provides explicit supervision across multiple spectral bands, emphasizing visually sensitive frequency components that are crucial for perceptual quality and prone to temporal jittering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FADRA recovers better facial structures and produces more temporally consistent videos than state-of-the-art methods, leading to clear gains in both quantitative metrics and visual perception.

AI.tldr: Introduces FADRA, a frequency-aware diffusion framework with iterative residual adaptation for robust video face restoration by leveraging a frozen diffusion backbone with LoRA adapters, LQ-guided residual refinement (RRAH), and a Frequency-Aware Loss to improve spatial fidelity and temporal coherence.
AI.motivation: Current video face restoration (VFR) methods struggle to balance spatial detail and temporal consistency under complex degradations; leveraging pre-trained diffusion models with lightweight adaptation and explicit frequency supervision can improve robustness.
AI.method: Freeze a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion model; apply lightweight LoRA adapters and a Low-Quality (LQ) Pixel-Alignment Feature Fusion module to adapt the frozen model to VFR. Introduce a Repeated Residual Adaptation Head (RRAH) for step-wise residual refinement after the diffusion backbone, guided by the degraded observation via LQ latent and current velocity. RRAH revisits LQ cues at each flow-matching step. Propose a Frequency-Aware Loss providing supervision across multiple spectral bands to emphasize perceptually important frequencies.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show FADRA yields better facial structure recovery and stronger temporal consistency than state-of-the-art methods, with clear gains in quantitative metrics and visual quality.
AI.conclusion: The approach effectively preserves temporal priors of the diffusion backbone while recovering fine details under challenging degradations, with frequency-aware supervision and LQ-guided residual adaptation enabling robust VFR.

title: Temporal Modeling of Optically Variable Devices in Identity Documents
comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2026)
summary: Robust remote verification of identity documents relies on analyzing faint, transparent security features like Optically Variable Devices (OVDs), or "holograms", within user-captured videos under uncontrolled conditions. Current systems, however, face critical limitations: existing methods often treat video frames in isolation, neglecting the intrinsic dynamic nature of OVDs and leaving systems vulnerable to swapping attacks, or focus on general holographic presence and lack the ability to verify specific OVD types. Moreover, the economic infeasibility of frame-by-frame video annotation makes supervised training impractical. In this work, we introduce two novel approaches for verifying the dynamic behavior of transparent OVDs protecting the holder's portrait, specifically designed for open-set scenarios where attack types are unknown during training. We demonstrate that these approaches can be trained without any attack samples in a self-supervised setting, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods on public datasets while adhering strictly to industrial constraints. Our results confirm that modeling temporal dynamics is essential for defeating sophisticated attacks under realistic conditions, and underscores the promise of sequence modeling and anomaly detection for OVD verification. Code is available at https://github.com/EPITAResearchLab/pouliquen.26.icdar.

AI.tldr: Two self-supervised, open-set approaches for verifying dynamic behavior of transparent OVDs in video sequences, outperforming prior methods on public datasets without attack annotations.
AI.motivation: Robust remote OVD verification is hindered by frame-wise processing, inability to model OVD dynamics, susceptibility to swapping, and impractical annotation for supervision.
AI.method: Two novel approaches that model the temporal dynamics of OVDs in video and perform anomaly detection for open-set attacks; trained fully self-supervised without attack samples.
AI.result: Empirical results show surpassing prior state-of-the-art on public datasets; demonstrates the necessity of temporal modeling; maintains practicality via self-supervision and open-set design; code released.
AI.conclusion: Modeling temporal dynamics and using anomaly detection enable robust OVD verification under realistic conditions and open-set attack spectra; promising for industrial deployment.

title: HoloCount: A Holistic Visual Counting Benchmark for MLLMs
summary: Visual counting is a fundamental pillar of multimodal intelligence, requiring a seamless integration of fine-grained grounding and spatial reasoning. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success in qualitative scene understanding, their quantitative precision remains a significant bottleneck, often characterized by persistent numerical hallucinations. Existing counting benchmarks primarily focus on basic perception in simplified contexts, failing to capture the complex failure modes that emerge under logical constraints or adversarial conditions. To address these limitations, we introduce HoloCount, a holistic and diagnostically rich benchmark structured around a three-level hierarchical taxonomy. HoloCount evaluates MLLMs across: (1) Semantic Counting, focusing on atomic and property-based enumeration; (2) Analytical Counting, assessing logical composition through spatial and set-based reasoning; and (3) Robustness Testing, probing model integrity against adverse scenarios and grounded counter-priors, such as high-density scenes and linguistic biases. Through an exhaustive evaluation of over 20 state-of-the-art MLLMs, we reveal a critical performance gap: even top-tier models degrade significantly as tasks transition from perception to complex analytical reasoning and adverse scenarios. Our findings provide a systematic landscape of current MLLM counting capabilities and offer a roadmap for developing more grounded and reliable multimodal systems. The dataset is available at https://mm-mvr.github.io/HoloCount/.

AI.tldr: HoloCount is a hierarchical benchmark for multimodal counting in MLLMs, covering semantic, analytical, and robustness aspects, revealing significant gaps in quantitative reliability across ~20 models.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs exhibit numerical hallucinations in counting; existing benchmarks focus on basic perception and miss complex logical constraints and adversarial scenarios. A diagnostically rich benchmark is needed.
AI.method: Introduce a three-level taxonomy (Semantic Counting, Analytical Counting, Robustness Testing), build the HoloCount dataset, and evaluate over 20 state-of-the-art MLLMs to characterize performance across levels and failure modes.
